h: How it works, in one paragraph
x: CrabbyTab  Welcome to the CrabbyTab wiki. This is the place to learn how to install CrabbyTab, run a debate tournament with it, and work on its code. CrabbyTab is a free, open-source debate tabulation system for British Parliamentary , two-team formats (Asian/UADC, Australs, World Schools, APDA, Karl Popper and custom) and N teams per room (for example public speaking). It handles the whole tournament: setup, participant imports, check-ins, draws, adjudicator and venue allocation, ballots, feedback, standings, breaks and elimination rounds, public pages, private URLs and email. Its algorithms follow Tabbycat 's. CrabbyTab is an independent project and is not affiliated with Tabbycat. Who it is for: tab directors, adjudication cores and organisers who want a capable tab system without paying for or maintaining a server. It runs on Vercel's and Firebase's free tiers. How it works, in one paragraph  CrabbyTab is local-first . The tab room's working copy lives in the browser (IndexedDB), and draws, allocations, standings and breaks are computed there, so the tab room keeps working on a flaky connection. For cloud tournaments, ballots, check-ins, draws and allocations sync live between administrator devices; other changes go up with Upload , which merges into Firebase Firestore and reports conflicting edits instead of overwriting them. A sanitised, cached snapshot of whatever you have released is then published for the public pages. Participants use private URLs (or optional public forms), which write to the cloud copy through server routes. See Backups, restore and cloud sync and Caching, indexing and performance . h: Trying it out without real data
x: Installation and local development  This page gets CrabbyTab running on your own machine. To put it online for a real tournament, continue with Deploying to Vercel and Firebase . Requirements  Node.js 22 ( package.json pins "node": "22.x" ). npm . package-lock.json is the authoritative lockfile. The repository also contains a bun.lock ; leave it alone unless you are deliberately changing package-manager conventions. A Firebase project with Authentication (email/password) and Cloud Firestore. Tournament data lives in your browser, but creating a tournament (including a demo tournament or a DebateXML import) needs a signed-in global administrator , and that needs Firebase Authentication plus server credentials. Without Firebase the hub shows Firebase is not configured . Optional: an SMTP server to try the email tools, staff invitations and registration emails. Install and run  git clone https://github.com/The-Studio-of-Sadiq/crabbytab.git cd crabbytab npm ci cp .env.example .env.local npm run dev Open http://localhost:3000 . The dev server always uses port 3000. Environment variables  Copy .env.example to .env.local and fill it in. Never commit .env.local . Variable Where it is used Purpose NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL Server (page metadata) Canonical base URL of the site. If empty it falls back to https://$VERCEL_URL on Vercel, otherwise http://localhost:3000 . NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY , _APP_ID , _AUTH_DOMAIN , _MEASUREMENT_ID , _MESSAGING_SENDER_ID , _PROJECT_ID , _STORAGE_BUCKET Browser The Firebase web-app config from Project settings → Your apps . These are public identifiers, not secrets. FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON Server only The full JSON of a Firebase service-account key, on one line. Escaped \n in the private key are converted back to newlines. If empty, the server falls back to Application Default Credentials. FIREBASE_ADMIN_UIDS Server only Firebase Authentication UIDs of global administrators , separated by commas or whitespace. See Staff and roles . SMTP_HOST , SMTP_PORT , SMTP_USER , SMTP_PASS , SMTP_FROM , SMTP_SECURE Server only Outgoing mail. SMTP_HOST , SMTP_USER , SMTP_PASS and SMTP_FROM are required for email; SMTP_PORT defaults to 587. SMTP_SECURE is true or false (TLS from the start of the connection); if empty, it is on only for port 465. EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET Server only, optional Shared secret for the signed delivery-status webhook ( POST /api/email/webhook ). Without it the endpoint answers 404. SMS_WEBHOOK_URL , SMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET Server only, optional A generic HTTPS SMS relay you control; each SMS is POSTed and signed with the secret. No SMS provider is built in. Details for the email and SMS variables: docs/email-notifications.md . Never put the service account, SMTP password or webhook secrets in a NEXT_PUBLIC_ variable — those are compiled into the browser bundle. Make yourself a global administrator  CrabbyTab has no public account sign-up. (The /register/{slug} pages are tournament registration forms for teams and adjudicators, not account creation.) Accounts are created in Firebase Authentication by hand, or by accepting a staff invitation from a tournament administrator. In the Firebase console, enable Authentication → Sign-in method → Email/Password and add a user. Copy that user's UID into FIREBASE_ADMIN_UIDS in .env.local . Provide server credentials ( FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON ). On every sign-in the server adds or removes the globalAdmin custom claim to match the list. Deploy the repository's firestore.rules to your project (see Deploying ). Restart npm run dev , sign in at /login and open /tournaments . You should now see Create a new tournament , Or import a DebateXML archive and Or load a demo tournament for a rehearsal . Trying it out without real data  Demo tournament: /tournaments → Or load a demo tournament for a rehearsal creates a seeded BP (24 teams) or WSDC (16 teams) practice tournament on this device. Its URL starts with demo- . See the First tournament walkthrough . Sample CSVs: the testdata/ folder contains small files (institutions, teams, adjudicators, venues, motions) for the import pages. See CSV formats . Useful scripts  Command What it does npm run dev Development server on port 3000 npm run build Production build (also type-checks application code) npm run start Serve the production build on port 3000 npm run test Run the Vitest suite once (no Firebase credentials needed) npm run lint next lint npx tsc --noEmit Full type check including tests CI ( .github/workflows/ci.yml ) runs npm ci , npm run lint , npx tsc --noEmit , npm run test and npm run build in that order. Run the same before opening a pull request. Details  The 1000-team scale benchmark runs inside npm run test with 2 rounds per format (about 20 s). Set CRABBYTAB_SCALE=full to play every round, or CRABBYTAB_SCALE=off to skip it. See docs/storage-and-scale.md . tools/tabbycat-diff compares CrabbyTab's draws, standings, breaks and allocations against recorded Tabbycat v2.12.1 output; its report runs in npm run test without Docker or Python. Regenerating Tabbycat's golden output needs Docker (or Python 3.11 and PostgreSQL); see its README. tools/i18n holds the translation tooling; see docs/internationalization.md . site/build.mjs renders these wiki pages into the static GitHub Pages site and checks every internal link and anchor ( --strict fails on a broken link). marked is not a project dependency; the script header explains how to point it at a separate install. The repository has no Firestore emulator setup, so firestore.rules are not executed in CI. Check rule changes in the Firebase console's Rules Playground before deploying them. Next steps  Deploying to Vercel and Firebase First tournament walkthrough Architecture if you want to change the code

h: Where reads and writes come from
How public caching keeps reads low
x: Deploying to Vercel and Firebase  CrabbyTab is designed to run for free: a Next.js app on Vercel and a Firebase project on the Spark (no-cost) plan. Nothing in the app needs a paid API. Very large events (around 1000 teams) may need Firebase's pay-as-you-go Blaze plan; see the read and write budget . You need: a GitHub fork or clone of the repository, a Vercel account, a Firebase project with Authentication (email/password) and Cloud Firestore , optionally an SMTP account for email. 1. Create the Firebase project  Create a project in the Firebase console . Authentication → Sign-in method: enable Email/Password . Under Settings → Authorized domains , add your Vercel URL and any custom domain. Firestore Database: create a database in production mode. Choose a region close to your users; it cannot be changed later. Project settings → Your apps: add a Web app and copy its config values into the NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_* variables. Project settings → Service accounts: generate a new private key. The downloaded JSON becomes FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON . Treat it as a secret. 2. Deploy the Firestore rules  The repository's firestore.rules are part of CrabbyTab's security model. They decide what tournament administrators, data-entry staff, global admins and signed-out visitors may read and write, and they deny every client access to server-only data (registrations, invitations, private-URL secrets). Without them the app does not work correctly and data may be exposed. The repository has no firebase.json , so deploy the rules in one of two ways: Console: paste the file into Firestore Database → Rules and press Publish . CLI: in a separate folder, create a minimal firebase.json such as { "firestore": { "rules": "firestore.rules" } } , copy firestore.rules next to it, and run firebase deploy --only firestore:rules --project <your-project-id> . Review the rules before publishing them, and redeploy them whenever you update CrabbyTab and the file has changed. The rules are not run in CI (there is no emulator setup), so check changes in the console's Rules Playground first; docs/live-collaboration.md lists the cases to try. See Security model for what the rules allow. No composite indexes need to be created by hand. If Firestore ever reports a missing index in the server logs, the error message contains a link that creates it. 3. Create the Vercel project  Import the repository in Vercel. The framework preset is Next.js ; the default install and build commands ( npm ci / npm run build ) work as they are. Set the Node.js version to 22.x . Add the environment variables (Production, and Preview if you test previews): Variable Required Notes NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_API_KEY , NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_APP_ID , NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_AUTH_DOMAIN , NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MEASUREMENT_ID , NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_MESSAGING_SENDER_ID , NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID , NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_STORAGE_BUCKET Yes Firebase web config. Public identifiers, compiled into the browser bundle, so a change needs a redeploy. FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON Yes Paste the whole JSON; it may stay on one line. Server only. FIREBASE_ADMIN_UIDS Yes UIDs of global administrators, comma or space separated. NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL Recommended Your production URL, used as the base for page metadata. Falls back to https://$VERCEL_URL . SMTP_HOST , SMTP_PORT , SMTP_USER , SMTP_PASS , SMTP_FROM , SMTP_SECURE For email Without them, everything except sending email works; invitation and registration links are then shown once to copy. EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET Optional Enables the signed delivery-status webhook. SMS_WEBHOOK_URL , SMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET Optional Your own HTTPS SMS relay. Variable details: Installation . Deploy. Server routes run on the Node.js runtime. The email send, retry and automatic-notification routes allow up to 60 seconds per request, and one email send is capped at 100 recipients. 4. Create accounts and global administrators  CrabbyTab has no public account sign-up . Create the first accounts in Firebase → Authentication → Users . Put the UIDs of the people who run the site into FIREBASE_ADMIN_UIDS . On every sign-in the server adds or removes the globalAdmin custom claim to match the list, and the Firestore rules trust that claim. After changing the variable, redeploy and have the person sign out and in again. Only global admins can create tournaments, load demo tournaments or import DebateXML archives. Tournament administrators and data-entry staff are added per tournament on its Staff page: either an existing account directly, or an email invitation , which lets the invitee create an account for exactly the invited address. See Staff and roles . Forgotten passwords are reset by email at /forgot-password (Firebase sends that email, not your SMTP server). 5. Email (optional)  Set the SMTP_* variables. Any SMTP provider works; check its daily sending limit against the size of your tournament. Send a test from the tournament's Email page. See Email and notifications . Staying inside the Spark budget  The Spark plan allows 50,000 Firestore document reads and 20,000 writes per day . CrabbyTab is built around those limits. Where reads and writes come from  Activity Firestore cost Public pages, projector, public check-ins, public schedule Almost none: served from cached snapshots (below). Audience size hardly matters. Opening a cloud tournament on an administrator device Reads every collection once, then live listeners take over. For a 100-team BP event with ~150 adjudicators that is a few hundred reads more. Live collaboration (administrator devices) Ballots, check-ins, draws and allocations are written record by record. Each change costs about one read per other listening admin device; a confirmed ballot about 3. Listeners cover the teams and adjudicators collections and the active round's debates and ballots only. Upload now Sends only records changed since this device last synced, in transactions of up to 150 records. An upload with nothing changed costs a handful of reads. Download and compare Reads the tournament's collections. Publishing public pages (after an upload or release) About one read per collection to check whether anything public changed; if so, one read of every public collection to rebuild the snapshot. Unchanged publishes are skipped. Private URLs (team, speaker and adjudicator portals) Participant-scoped: a team portal reads its own debates, their teams and ballots (around 10 debates, not the whole draw). Registration form 2 reads per page view (cached 30 s at the edge); a submission about 7 reads and 5 writes. A rough guide: four administrator devices on a 100-team event stay well inside 50k reads a day. A 1000-team event's first upload is about 10,000 writes, so several full uploads a day exceed Spark's 20,000 writes; plan on Blaze for events of that size. Details: docs/storage-and-scale.md and docs/live-collaboration.md . How public caching keeps reads low  Public pages never read the tournament collections. When an administrator uploads or releases something, the browser builds a sanitised public projection (only released data) and publishes it to publicViews/{slug} , split into sections and one section per public round. The server reads snapshots through the Next.js Data Cache , which Vercel shares across instances. A publish invalidates the tournament's cache at once. Otherwise the root document is refreshed hourly and section documents daily. The CDN absorbs bursts. GET /api/public/tournaments/{slug} and /checkins answer with Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, s-maxage=15, stale-while-revalidate=30 ; /version with 10 / 20 seconds. A single round requested with its current content hash ( ?round={id}&h={hash} ) is cached for a day, because that URL never changes meaning. Clients poll a tiny version marker. The public page and the projector check /version every 45 seconds and reload only the rounds whose hash changed. The public check-in page refreshes every 30 seconds through the same cache. Other public endpoints are cached too: the schedule JSON for 2 minutes, the iCalendar feed and public audit status for a minute, and the cross-tournament motion statistics for 10 minutes. A tournament that has never been published is built once from its collections on first view and cached for 5 minutes. For large events, publish before sharing links. Republish by hand from the account menu with Republish public pages . It publishes the cloud copy; if this device has changes that are not uploaded, it asks whether to upload first. Updating a deployment  Pull the new version and read the commit log. Compare firestore.rules and .env.example with your deployment and update both if they changed. Redeploy on Vercel. Ask organisers to Upload now before the update (so nothing is only on one device), and to reload afterwards. Checklist  Email/password sign-in enabled, authorised domain added Firestore created and firestore.rules published Vercel env vars set (Firebase web config, service account, admin UIDs), Node.js 22 A global admin can sign in and sees Create a new tournament (Optional) SMTP configured and a test email sent from the Email page (Optional) A test tournament uploaded and its public tab opened in a private window

h: Option A: rehearse with a demo tournament
x: First tournament walkthrough  A complete run through a small tournament, from setup to the final, with the current interface. It assumes CrabbyTab is deployed (or running locally ) and that you are a global administrator. Sidebar sections are written as Section → Page . How saving works. Everything you do is saved in this browser at once. Once the tournament has a cloud copy, ballots, check-ins, draws and allocations also sync live to other administrator devices. Settings, rounds, motions, rooms, breaks and feedback reach the cloud with Upload now (cloud status menu in the top bar), and release buttons upload and publish in one step. The top bar shows how many changes are not uploaded. Option A: rehearse with a demo tournament  The fastest way to learn the workflow, and to train volunteers. /tournaments → Or load a demo tournament for a rehearsal . Choose British Parliamentary (24 teams) or WSDC (16 teams, three speakers and a reply) and a URL starting with demo- , then Create demo tournament . It comes with institutions, teams and speakers (some ESL), adjudicators with scores and conflicts, rooms, preliminary and elimination rounds, motions and Open / ESL break categories, under that format's rules preset. It has no draws or results. Follow Each preliminary round below for Round 1: generate the draw, allocate, release. Admin → Rehearsal tools : pick the round and a seed, then Simulate results (one random, valid, confirmed ballot per debate) and Simulate feedback . The same seed on the same draw gives the same results. Simulated records are marked "Simulated (rehearsal)". Repeat for every round, then generate the break and run the eliminations. Rehearsal tools also work on a real tournament, but then each run needs the tournament's short name typed as confirmation and is recorded in the audit log. Never use them during an event. Option B: a real tournament  Before the tournament  Create the tournament. /tournaments → Create a new tournament . The wizard asks for the name and URL slug (it cannot change later), the format, an optional Tabbycat rules preset (Australs, BP, UADC, WSDC, APDA, Karl Popper and others), scoring, the number of preliminary rounds and draw method, break categories, what is public and how participants submit ballots. See Tournament setup and formats . Review settings. Admin → Configuration : Draw rules , Round settings , Format & teams , Scoring & ballots , Standings rules , Public visibility . Defaults follow Tabbycat's ( Settings reference ). To copy another tournament's settings, use Format & teams → Configuration file and rules presets . Break and speaker categories. Results → Break : check the categories (add ESL, Novice…). Setup → Speaker categories : add speaker categories if eligibility depends on them. Import participants ( how ): Setup → Institutions , Teams , Adjudicators (each with Import CSV and a preview), then Venues and Motions . Try the files in testdata/ when rehearsing. Check adjudicators. Base scores, trainees, Adjudication core , Breaking and Tester flags, and conflicts (adjudicator dialog, or Setup → Conflicts ). Rooms. Setup → Venues : priorities, categories, capacities; Setup → Room preferences for soft preferences ( details ). Upload. Cloud status menu → Upload now . This creates the cloud copy, claims the slug and switches on live sync for ballots, check-ins and draws. Staff. Admin → Assistants (the staff page): add tournament administrators and data-entry staff, by existing account or email invitation ( Staff and roles ). Registration (optional). Setup → Registration to let teams and adjudicators register themselves, with representative links and team invitations. Private URLs. Public → Private URLs : Ensure all credentials assigned , then Print QR slips or email the links ( how ). Schedule (optional). Setup → Schedule : start times, parallel panels, preparation time, the public schedule. Back up. Account menu → Export tournament backup , and keep the file safe. Each preliminary round  Select the round in the top bar; the sidebar group becomes Round · R1 . Availability. Round · R1 → Availability . Everyone is present unless marked absent. Mark absentees, use barcode scanning, or let participants self check-in ( how ). Draw. Round · R1 → Draw . Check the draw type in Draw setup (the first power-paired round is random), then Generate R1 draw . Read the draw check and the flags (rematches, same institution, side counts, pull-ups); move teams by drag or Move → Place here / Swap here ; mark postponed debates. If teams are short of a full room, add a swing team or let byes apply. ( Rounds and draws ) Rooms. Rooms are assigned when the draw is generated; press Allocate venues after changes. Adjudicators. Round · R1 → Allocation . Set panel size and feedback weight, optionally Prioritise by bracket / by liveness , then Auto-Allocate All . Fix the reported clashes by hand. ( Adjudicator allocation ) Confirm and release the draw. On the Draw page: Confirm draw (optional; locks the matchups), Release to teams only (optional; teams see their room on their private URL without the panel), then Release draw to public . Then Reveal Adjudicators on the Allocation page. Put Display on the projector. Motions. Setup → Motions : release the round's info slides, then its motions, when announced. Releasing motions starts the preparation time if one is set. Ballots. Adjudicators submit ballots from their private URLs (or the public ballot form, if chosen), or the tab room enters paper ballots on Results (track paper with the ballot intake board). Confirm each ballot; with double entry on, a different person checks it. ( Ballots and results ) Publish and complete. On Results : Publish round results and, separately, Publish team speaks (skip for silent rounds), then Complete round . Completed rounds count towards break liveness, and the tabs cover completed rounds only. (The next round's power pairing needs every ballot of this round confirmed.) Feedback. Results → Feedback : review submissions and the progress panel; lower the next round's feedback weight if base scores should keep influence ( Feedback ). Back up after each round. The break  After the last preliminary round, check Results → Standings . Results → Break : set overrides (ineligible, withdrawn, resolved ties) and Generate break for each category, highest priority first. Ties at the cutoff are reported and must be resolved with overrides. Check Breaking adjudicators too. Release the break from the Public release panel on Results → Standings . ( Breaks and eliminations ) Elimination rounds  Select the first elimination round and Generate draw on the Draw page: a seeded bracket from the break (partial eliminations give the top seeds a bye). Sides follow Sides in elimination rounds (by seed, or random and recorded on the ballot). Allocate panels, release the draw, reveal adjudicators, enter and confirm ballots as before. On Results , Proceed to next round marks losing teams eliminated and activates the next elimination round. Afterwards  Results → Standings → Public release : Release the tab releases the team and speaker tabs, the motion tab, scoresheets and every round's results together; or release items one by one (participants, adjudicator lists, speaker category tabs…). Release the audit log for transparency ( Admin → Audit log ). Export a final backup and a DebateXML archive (account menu). Gotchas  Generating a draw while an earlier round is unfinished asks for a reason: unfinished results do not count towards power pairing. Regenerating a draw that has ballots discards them (they stay in history). Confirmed or released draws need a reason to regenerate. A changed panel hides revealed adjudicators again; reveal again when done. Changing the format, speakers or ballot mode is locked once ballots exist. Self check-ins and participants' ballots go to the cloud; a device with live sync paused sees them only after Download and compare .

h: Configuration file and rules presets for an existing tournament
x: Tournament setup and formats  This page covers creating a tournament, the debate formats, Tabbycat rules presets and moving settings between tournaments. Every individual setting is listed in the Settings reference . Who can create tournaments  Only global administrators (see Staff and roles ) can create tournaments. On the Tournaments hub ( /tournaments ) they see three ways to start: Option Page Creates Create a new tournament /tournaments/new An empty tournament from the setup wizard (below). Or import a DebateXML archive (from Tabbycat or CrabbyTab) /tournaments/import A new tournament from a DebateXML file. See Participants and imports . Or load a demo tournament for a rehearsal /tournaments/demo A seeded practice tournament (BP with 24 teams, or WSDC with 16 teams). See First tournament walkthrough . The same choices are in the tournament switcher in the top bar ( New tournament , Import tournament , Load demo tournament ). Other users see the tournaments they are assigned to. A new tournament is saved on this device only ("Upload it to Firestore only when you choose to"). It reaches the cloud, the public pages, registration and other staff after the first Upload now (cloud status menu in the top bar). Supported formats  Format Teams per room Speakers Replies Default speaker / reply scale Default team precedence British Parliamentary (BP) 4 2 No 50–100 Points, total speaks, firsts, seconds, thirds Asian Parliamentary (UADC) 2 3 Yes 70–80 / 35–40 Points, total speaks, total margin Australs 2 3 Yes 70–80 / 35–40 as UADC World Schools (WSDC) 2 3 Yes 60–80 / 30–40 as UADC Custom two-team 2 3 (any 1–6) Yes (optional) 68–84 / 34–42 as UADC N teams per room (public speaking) any whole number except 2 and 4 (default 6) 1 No 50–99 Average speaks All score steps default to 1. New tournaments start with a power-paired draw, balanced sides, no double entry, motion vetoes on, the draw / results / standings / motions public, and feedback on (1–10). What the format decides  BP uses its own position-balancing draw (Hungarian assignment), one consensus ballot per debate (BP voting ballots are not offered), and elimination rounds where two of four teams advance. Two-team formats add voting ballots, forfeits, seeded and round-robin draws with team seeds, preallocated sides, sides chosen on the ballot (coin toss), and Tabbycat's AIDA break rules. N teams per room follows Tabbycat's scope for these counts: random and manual draws only, ballots that record scores (and, in elimination rounds, which teams advance), no side rules, and no generated elimination draws. The setup wizard creates no elimination rounds; add them later and draw them by hand. When the field does not divide evenly, a random draw puts the remainder in a short last room (or gives byes, with an automatic bye method). See Rounds and draws . The setup wizard  Create a new tournament opens a seven-step wizard. Next checks each step; Create tournament re-checks every step. Basics — Tournament name (at least 3 characters), Short name (optional, up to 15) and URL slug . The slug is suggested from the name. It must be 3–40 lowercase letters, numbers and single hyphens, must not be a reserved word ( account , api , forgot-password , invite , login , register , tournaments , public , display , private , new , admin ) or already used on this device, and cannot be changed later . It becomes the tournament's address, e.g. /my-open-2026/public . Format — one of the six formats above (for N teams per room , also Teams per room ), and an optional Tabbycat rules preset (next section). Scoring — Substantive speakers per team (1–6), speaker score range and step, whether reply speeches are scored, and the reply range. Rounds — Number of preliminary rounds (1–20); Draw method : Power-paired (Swiss), Random or Round robin; Side allocation : Balanced, Random, or Chosen on the ballot (two-team only); Require double entry of ballots . With power pairing, Round 1 is created as a random draw (or seeded, under the APDA preset). N teams per room always uses random draws and skips the side choice. Choosing round robin also turns off history and institution avoidance and sets the team import to numeric seeds, as Tabbycat's round-robin presets do. Breaks — break categories with Name , Teams that break , Reserve size and General (open) break . Default: Open , 8 teams, 2 reserves. No categories means preliminary rounds only. BP break sizes must be even and at least 4. Public & feedback — which of the draw, motions, results and standings are public; Public information options (Tabbycat's preset for online events: the current round's draw, break categories, results, motions and team standings); Participant data entry (how adjudicators and teams submit ballots and feedback: Default , Private URLs , Public forms or Tab staff only ); and whether to collect adjudicator feedback, with its score range. Review — a summary and the list of rounds that will be created. The wizard creates the preliminary rounds plus the elimination rounds needed for the largest break: two-team ⌈log₂(break size)⌉ rounds, BP ⌈log₂(break size / 4)⌉ + 1 rounds (none for N teams per room ). They are named Grand Final, Semifinals, Quarterfinals, Octofinals, Double and Triple Octofinals, then Elimination N . Break sizes that do not halve cleanly (for example 12) start with a partial elimination round in which the top seeds get byes. Everything except the slug can be changed later under Admin → Configuration . Rules presets  A rules preset applies the settings that the Tabbycat preset of the same name sets: format, speakers, score scale, ballot mode, motion settings, draw rules, standings precedence and, for some, feedback paths and public options. Settings you edit in the wizard afterwards win. Recommended order  Break categories (Results → Break ) and speaker categories (Setup → Speaker categories), so imports can refer to them. Institutions — teams and adjudicators are linked by institution name or code. Teams Adjudicators — an adjudicator linked to an institution (and not marked independent) automatically conflicts with it. Venues , Room preferences and Motions . Conflicts (CSV or by hand). Exact column names and aliases: CSV formats . Sample files are in testdata/ . Importing institutions, teams and adjudicators (CSV)  On the Institutions, Teams or Adjudicators page, choose Import CSV , upload a file or paste text, then Preview import . Nothing is saved until you press Import . The preview lists every row with what will happen: Errors (row cannot be imported): missing name, invalid email, score or yes/no flag, unknown break category, a speaker email or categories without a speaker name, wrong number of cells. A file with errors is refused unless you tick Import the valid rows only . Warnings : no speakers (placeholder speakers "Team Speaker 1"… are created; rename them), fewer speakers than the format uses, a speaker email already used, an adjudicator with the same name at another institution. Duplicates are detected instead of created twice. Institutions match by name or code, teams by name, adjudicators by email (else name and institution). A match defaults to Skip ; switch it to Update existing (only filled cells change; speakers keep their ids) or Create . New institutions named in the file are listed with a suggested code you can edit; untick one to keep the name as text without linking it. Independent , Unaffiliated , None and - mean no institution. New speaker categories named in speakerN_categories are created (not public) and listed. Columns that will be ignored are listed. Whole-file problems stop the import: files over 5 MB, an empty file, a header with no rows, repeated column names, a missing name column or an unclosed quote. Formulas and markup are kept as text, never evaluated. Team seeds. The Team seed column setting at the top of the team import decides what a seed column means: Do not ask (default; the column is ignored), a number (0–99,999, higher is stronger) or a seed title (Unseeded, Free seed, Half seed, Full seed). Seeds are used by seeded and round-robin draws. Venues and motions import directly from CSV, without this preview. Each import is one audit-log event. For cloud tournaments, teams and adjudicators are written live like any other edit. Teams  Setup → Teams lists every team with links to its private URL and its team record . Add team or the edit button opens the team dialog: Team name and Institution affiliation (or Unaffiliated / independent : no institutional clash constraints). Tabbycat name (optional): build the name from a reference, see below. Composite team : speakers from more than one institution, see below. Code name and Emoji , shown publicly when code names are on. Break eligibility for each non-general break category (every team is in the general ones). Speakers : name, email, speaker categories, code name, last name, pronoun and Anonymous on public pages . Add speaker adds a slot; Remove removes one. Set elsewhere: seeds on the Draw page (or the CSV seed column), divisions from the CSV division / division_id columns, venue requirements from the CSV requirement columns. Adding and removing speakers  A speaker can be removed only if they have no speeches on a live ballot, a score or any adjudicator's scoresheet. Otherwise the button is disabled with the reason, and the save is refused (also through the API). Rename the speaker instead, or discard those ballots first. Team names: references and prefixes  A team can be named the Tabbycat way: a reference ("1", "A"), an optional short reference , and Prefix with the institution . Its long name is "institution name + reference" ("Victoria 1"); its short name "institution code + short reference" ("VUW 1"). Admin → Configuration → Format & teams → Team names chooses which one teams show, offers Update team names after an institution is renamed, and Preview conversion to convert existing teams (a team called "Auckland 1" from Auckland becomes reference "1" with the prefix on). Teams without a reference keep the name as typed. Composite teams  Tick Speakers from more than one institution and the other institutions. A composite team is an ordinary team in draws, standings and breaks; its other institutions count as its own for same-institution draw avoidance and for adjudicator institution conflicts. (A swing team, which stands in for a missing team in one round, is different; see Rounds and draws .) Code names and emoji  Admin → Configuration → Public visibility sets the Team code names mode (off, real names with code names as tooltips, code names publicly, code names everywhere) and Speaker and adjudicator code names . The same page reports how many teams lack a code name or emoji and offers Generate missing code names ( Code name standard : emoji names or speakers' last names) and Assign missing emoji . Under code-name modes only the code name leaves the server; a team without one appears without a name. Setup → Code names lists each team's code name next to its real name, institution and speakers. Teams added by hand get no code name automatically, and saving a team clears a code name that equals its own real name. Team record  Each team row links to /{slug}/team/{teamId} (administrators): details and speakers, private URL, every debate including unreleased results and unconfirmed ballots, the panel and each speech, adjudicator conflicts with the reason, and feedback the team submitted. Speakers  Speakers carry name, email, speaker categories, code name, optional last name (used by the last-name code-name generator; otherwise the last word of the name) and optional pronoun (printed after the name on ballots, e.g. "Alex Kim (they/them)"). Phone and gender can also come from registration. Pronouns, last names, phones and emails are never published. Speaker categories (Setup → Speaker categories): name, slug, order, Public tab and Public limit . A category can be deleted only when no speaker is in it. Break eligibility can be derived from speaker categories on Results → Break → Eligibility. Older free-text speaker labels are shown as "From labels, not saved" until the list is saved. Adjudicators  The adjudicator dialog holds: name, institution (or independent), email, Base rating (1–10) , Trainee judge , Adjudication core , Breaking adjudicator , Tester (always on for the adjudication core), Anonymous on public pages , gender, region, code name, last name, pronoun, and Conflicts (team, adjudicator and other institution conflicts). Test scores, base-score history and the tester and breaking columns are also on the Feedback pages. Each adjudicator's name links to their adjudicator record (rounds and roles, scores and history, feedback received, conflicts) for administrators and staff with feedback or score access. See Adjudicator allocation for how conflicts are used. Institutions and coaches  An institution has a name, code, region and optional venue requirements. Its dialog also lists coaches and representatives (name and email). Coaches are organiser-only and receive emails sent to the Institution coaches and representatives group. Registration → Representatives → Save representatives as coaches copies every active representative into their institution's coaches. Conflicts  Setup → Conflicts (administrators and staff with conflict access): Import conflicts from CSV. Each row fills exactly two of adjudicator , team , institution , other_adjudicator : adjudicator–team, adjudicator–adjudicator, adjudicator–institution or team–institution. Unknown or ambiguous names are errors; conflicts already recorded are skipped. Preview first, as with the participant imports. Recorded conflicts lists every conflict and removes one (adjudicator–adjudicator conflicts from both sides). Add a team–institution conflict : adjudicators from that institution should not judge the team. Export conflicts CSV . Conflicts are never shown publicly. Diversity and institution reports  Diversity is an inline editor for speaker and adjudicator gender and region (administrators; saved when you leave a field), with summary statistics and gender by institution (speakers by their team's institution; independent adjudicators excluded). Genders are free text, grouped ignoring case and spaces. Diversity is shown as badges on the Allocation page; it is not an allocation constraint. Adjudicator requirement shows teams and adjudicators per institution, registered and per drawn preliminary round (chairs, panellists, trainees). An institution with N teams that provides fewer than N−1 adjudicators is flagged with an icon and text. Registration  Setup → Registration (administrators; the tournament must be uploaded first) lets teams, adjudicators and institutions register on a public form at /register/{slug} . Nothing a registrant submits reaches the tournament directly unless you choose automatic acceptance. Settings : accept registrations and an optional window; which kinds may register and through which channel (open form, representative links); speakers per team; speaker categories offered; per-institution and tournament-wide limits; custom questions (also per speaker, for institutions and for coaches); per-form messages; generated team names and code names; which person fields are asked; confirmation ( Always , Only open registrations , Never ). Optional team fields (none by default): Prefix the team name with the institution , break categories (non-general ones), seed (number or seed title, following the team import's seed setting) and emoji . The break-category list and seed mode are copied when the settings are saved, so save them again after changing break categories. Representatives : give an institution's representative a personal link that fixes the institution and shows the places left. New link replaces it, Revoke stops it. Representatives can request place transfers, which you approve on this tab. Team invitations (Representatives tab): a link for one existing team ( /register/{slug}/join#… ), shown once to copy, through which speakers add themselves to that team. New link replaces it, Withdraw stops it. Joining needs no review, but respects the registration window, the maximum speakers per team, and refuses a repeated name or email. Review queue : each submission with possible duplicates flagged; Approve creates the team or adjudicator (with private URL keys, matching or creating the institution), Edit , Reject (optional reason, not emailed), Reopen . Use Refresh to see new submissions. With Email registrants on (Email page), registrants get "Registration received" and "Registration approved" emails. Full details, limits and abuse protection: docs/registration.md . Deleting  Deleting a team, adjudicator, institution, venue, motion or break category asks for confirmation. Records still in use cannot be deleted: Record Refused while referenced by Instead Team a debate (including a bye), a ballot or feedback Mark the team unavailable Adjudicator a panel, a ballot or feedback Mark the adjudicator unavailable Venue a debate Mark the venue unavailable Institution a team or adjudicator Move or delete those first Break category a generated break or a drawn elimination round — For cloud tournaments, deleted teams and adjudicators are soft-deleted in Firestore at once (content kept); other records are queued as cloud deletions for the next upload. DebateXML import  Tournaments hub → Or import a DebateXML archive (global administrators) creates a new tournament from a DebateXML file, such as a Tabbycat export or a CrabbyTab archive. It never merges into an existing tournament. Choose the file (up to 10 MB). It is validated before anything is saved. Imported: institutions, teams and speakers (categories, gender), adjudicators (score, trainee, independent, gender, conflicts), venues, motions with info slides, break and speaker categories, divisions, feedback questions, rounds, debates with sides and panels, results (consensus or voting), byes and confirmed feedback. Check-ins and availability  Availability decides which teams are drawn and which adjudicators are allocated in a round. It is managed on the round's Availability page (sidebar → Round · R1 → Availability , /{slug}/checkins ). Administrators and staff with the check-in permission can use it. How availability works  Teams and adjudicators are available or absent per round . A per-round value overrides the older tournament-wide check-in flag. Anyone with no availability record counts as available. Imported and newly added participants are therefore present by default. Mark people absent to leave them out. (Tabbycat works the other way round: nobody is in until checked in.) Check-in expiry ( Admin → Configuration → Public visibility → Check-in expiry , hours; 0 = never, the default): a timestamped check-in older than this no longer counts. Records without a timestamp are unaffected. The draw uses team availability. Allocation uses adjudicator availability unless Skip adjudicator check-ins is on ( Configuration → Draw rules ). Rooms have their own availability (default and per round, set on Setup → Venues) and a check-in tick; see Venues and constraints . Swing teams are available only in the rounds they were created or reused for. The Availability page  Pick the round at the top. The page shows: Tabs Teams (present/total) , Adjudicators (present/total) and Venues (present/total) , each with a search box and a per-row Present / Absent toggle. Expired check-ins are marked Expired ; each row shows when it was checked in. Speakers under each team, each with their own check-in toggle (see below). Mark all present . Copy availability from R(n−1) : everyone without an explicit setting for this round gets their availability in the previous round (present or absent). Mark breaking adjudicators present : checks in every adjudicator flagged Breaking . Print barcode labels : Code 39 labels for teams, speakers, adjudicators and venues. Barcode check-in : a scan box and, where supported, Use camera . Check-in history : the round's 25 most recent changes, with the source (tab room, barcode, bulk, self check-in) and who made them. Public status : a link to the public check-in page. Speaker check-in  Each speaker can be checked in for a round (toggle on the Teams tab, or scan the speaker's barcode). When every speaker of a team is in, the team becomes available. Checking a speaker out does not withdraw the team; mark the team absent for that. Barcodes and scanners  Scan with a USB or keyboard-wedge scanner into the scan box (most type the code and press Enter); you can also paste an id. The code is matched to a team, speaker, adjudicator or venue, and that record is checked in for the selected round. Unknown codes show No team, adjudicator, or venue matches that barcode. Use camera works in browsers with the BarcodeDetector API; otherwise use a USB scanner. What other devices see  For cloud tournaments, team and adjudicator availability is live on administrator devices: a check-in made on one device reaches the others within seconds, and goes into the queue while offline. Data-entry staff's check-ins reach administrators when the staff device syncs. Two devices changing different rounds never undo each other; the same field changed on both is last-write-wins. Room availability still travels with Upload now . Self check-in  With Self check-in from private URLs on ( Configuration → Public visibility ), team and adjudicator private URLs show a check-in panel for the current check-in round : the earliest round that is neither cancelled nor completed. Participants mark themselves present or absent. Requests are passcode-checked and rate-limited, and refused for any other round. The API offers the same as PUT /me/checkin . Self check-ins are written to the cloud copy. A live administrator device receives them within seconds. A device that is not live sees them after Download and compare or a reload; if that device changed the same participant in the meantime, the participant is listed as a sync conflict for you to resolve rather than being silently overwritten. Public check-in status  With Public check-in counts on ( Configuration → Public visibility ), /{slug}/checkins/public shows, per round, how many teams and adjudicators are present out of the total. When the participants list is also public, it lists each team and adjudicator with whether they are checked in for a chosen round. Names follow the public naming rules (team code names, participant code names; anonymous adjudicators are counted but not listed). The page refreshes every 30 seconds from the published public snapshot, so changes appear after the next publish (an upload or release). Data-entry staff  Data-entry staff with the check-in permission can use the Availability page; speaker check-ins change the team's speakers, so they also need the participant-editing permission. Their changes reach the cloud when their device syncs. Details  Every change made on the page or by self check-in is recorded on the record itself (time, round, present/absent, source and the staff member's name), at most 50 entries per record; the server appends self check-ins without that cap. Room check-in expiry ( Configuration → Public visibility ) marks rooms checked in longer ago than that as expired. It does not change whether a room is allocated. Availability is exported with Admin → Data exports → Availability (every team, adjudicator and venue × every round). API: availability and check-in endpoints under /rounds/{seq}/availabilities and /…/checkin ( write:checkins ); speaker check-in through the API checks in the whole team. See API and tokens . Rounds and draws  This page is the organiser's guide to rounds, the schedule and the draw. The algorithms follow Tabbycat's draw generators; the full description, with every difference from Tabbycat, is in docs/draw-generation.md and docs/rounds-schedule-and-motions.md . Rounds  The setup wizard creates the preliminary rounds plus the elimination rounds needed for the largest break (Grand Final, Semifinals, Quarterfinals, Octofinals, Double and Triple Octofinals, then Elimination N ). Afterwards: Add a round: round menu in the top bar → New round… ( Round name , Abbreviation , Round stage : preliminary or elimination). Rounds are added after the existing ones. Change the number of preliminary rounds: Admin → Configuration → Round settings → Number of preliminary rounds (0–20) → Update round count . Lowering it cancels rounds (a round with ballots cannot be cancelled; one with a draw needs a reason); raising it restores cancelled rounds first. Cancelled rounds are ignored by standings, completion and the public pages. Delete a round: Round settings → Delete an individual round . This permanently deletes its debates and ballots and unassigns its motions. It needs a reason if the round has ballots or a later round was drawn after it, and is refused for an advanced elimination round. Round settings also has Feedback by round (switch feedback on or off per round) and Points weight by round (team points earned in the round are multiplied by its weight; default 1). Elimination rounds always use the elimination draw type, and only elimination rounds can; a round where stage and draw type do not fit is refused. The schedule and concurrent rounds  Setup → Schedule has four parts: Rounds and start times: each round's Slot and Starts at . Rounds of the same stage in the same slot run concurrently (for example "Round 1 (A)" and "Round 1 (B)"). Parallel preliminary panels: Rounds per slot → Group preliminary rounds groups the preliminary rounds into slots of that size, renaming default names to "Round k (A)", "Round k (B)". Existing rounds are only regrouped when you press the button; rounds added later follow the setting. Preparation time (minutes): releasing a round's motions sets its start to release time plus preparation time. Debate times: give individual debates their own start time. Tournament schedule: events with types, published with Publish schedule to /{slug}/schedule/public , as JSON and as an iCalendar feed. Rules for concurrent rounds: Power pairing waits only for rounds in earlier slots. History (rematches, sides, adjudicator history) comes from earlier slots only. Draw generation leaves out rooms already used by a concurrent round; auto-allocation leaves out adjudicators and rooms already used by one. Publishing a draw that shares a team, adjudicator or room with a concurrent round needs a recorded reason ( concurrent_round_clash ). Draw, Allocation, Results and Availability show a Running at the same time bar to switch between concurrent rounds and see their progress and clashes. The projector shows every concurrent round of the shown slot together. The current round  By default the current round is derived: the latest round whose draw is released to the public. The Draw page shows Current round: … (automatic) . Make {round} current sets it by hand; public pages (the "current round only" draw mode, the round they open on, public ballot forms), the projector and private URLs then use that round and the rounds of its slot. Use automatic current round clears it. Setting it never publishes an unreleased draw and, unlike Tabbycat, does not mark rounds complete or incomplete. Self check-in uses its own rule (the earliest round that is neither cancelled nor completed); see Check-ins and availability . Allocate venues Draw page → Allocate venues See Venues and constraints . Confirm draw (optional) Draw page Confirmed, not released : tab room only; regenerating or re-pairing needs a reason. Release to teams only (optional) Draw page Each team's private URL shows its room, side and opponents without the panel. Release draw to public Draw page Public pages (if Public draw is on), projector, adjudicators' private URLs and remote ballots. Reveal Adjudicators Allocation page Panels become visible to teams and the public. Release motions Setup → Motions Not released , Info slides released or Motions released . Draft edits are saved on this device and, for cloud tournaments, sent live to other administrator devices (debates are live; the round's stage travels with the upload). The Draw page  Sidebar → Round · R1 → Draw (administrators). Pick the round with Select round . Below the stage controls, the Draw setup for {round} panel offers: Draw type for this round: Power-paired , Random , Seeded (by team seed) , Round robin or Manual (empty rooms) . It applies the next time the draw is generated. Power-paired rounds with no results yet are drawn at random. Team seeds (seeded and round-robin draws; seed titles when the team import uses them) → Save seeds . Preallocated sides for this round, when the side rule is Preallocated → Save sides . Division (when teams have divisions): "This round will draw only teams in the selected division". The Side pre-allocations, all preliminary rounds grid (two-team formats with preallocated sides, on preliminary rounds) shows every team × round: rounds without a draw are editable, drawn rounds show the side each team took. Generate random sides for every round without a draw fills it (each round half affirmative, each team's affirmative count within one of the others'; the seed is in the audit log), and Copy sides from a previous round applies the same or opposite sides from a drawn round. The Swing teams panel appears when the available teams do not fill the last room (see Swing teams ). Generating: Generate {round} draw , or Manually build rooms for empty rooms. Draws run in a background worker, so the page stays usable; a Cancel button stops a long job and saves nothing. If the round changed while computing, nothing is saved and you are asked to try again. After generating , each room card shows the venue (with its link), bracket, live teams, room rank, Sides on ballot when applicable, the draw check's problems and warnings, a Postponed switch (with optional reason) and the debate's venue requirements. Header actions: Add room , Allocate venues , Draw details , Export CSV (draw with adjudicators and motion), Print draw sheet , and a filter by room or team. Draw check and flags  The draw check lists problems (must fix or override to release) and warnings. Each team carries flags; hover or focus one for the full sentence: Flag Meaning Met R2, R4 Rematch, with the rounds they met in Same institution Both teams share an institution (composite teams count all their institutions) AFF ×2, NEG ×1 (BP: each position) Sides so far, including sides recorded on ballots AFF ×3 (warning) This round would leave the team that many times on one side, two or more above its least-used side Pulled up , Pulled up ×N before Pulled up into this bracket; earlier pull-ups Swing A swing team, not ranked Draw details lists each team's points, this round's room and opponents, sides by round ( TBC when chosen on the ballot), previous opponents, side counts and pull-ups, plus Tabbycat's generator flags: One-up-one-down (history / institution / to accommodate) , Bubble up / Bubble down (…) , Can't bubble up/down and Too many swaps . For BP rounds after the first it also shows the position balance report : each team's OG/OO/CG/CO counts before and after, the position cost, and whether the team became balanced or imbalanced. Editing a draw  Drag teams between slots, rooms and the Unassigned teams pool , or use the keyboard and touch equivalent: Move picks a team, then Place here / Swap here on a slot, or Return picked team to pool . Arrow keys, Home and End move between targets; Escape cancels. Every move is announced to screen readers. A team moved to another room loses its pull-up mark. Once a debate has a live ballot, its teams and sides cannot change (discard the ballot first), and its panel changes need a reason. Re-pairing a confirmed or released draw needs a reason too. Changing rooms and venue requirements never does. Manual venue choices refuse rooms that are unavailable, already used or unsuitable.
