Not on public pages, the projector or adjudicators' private URLs; no remote ballots yet. Release draw to public , Unrelease draw Released to public Public pages (per the public draw mode), projector, adjudicators' private URLs, remote ballots Unrelease draw (back to Confirmed ) Releasing to teams or to the public runs the draw check: errors need a recorded reason, warnings never block. Going on from teams-only to public does not re-check what teams already saw. Releases and unreleases upload and republish; confirming and unconfirming are saved on this device and reach other devices with the next upload. Difference from Tabbycat: Tabbycat's public draw page also lists teams-only releases without adjudicators; CrabbyTab shows them only on team private URLs. Draw types  Draw type Formats Notes Power-paired Two-team, BP Brackets by the first team-standings metric (team points by default). Before any results, drawn as random. Random All Two-team: shuffled, then clashes removed by swaps or minimum-cost matching (per conflict avoidance). BP: institutions spread across rooms, positions balanced. N teams per room: dealt into rooms in order. Seeded Two-team, BP Teams ordered by seed, highest first. Two-team: one bracket with the configured pairing and conflict avoidance. BP: one bracket placed by position history. Every team needs a seed. Round robin Two-team, BP Two-team: Tabbycat's Berger schedule by seed (seed 1 first). BP: Tabbycat's tables for 16 teams (5 rounds) and 28 teams (9 rounds); seeds must be exactly 1..N. More rounds than one cycle, or other team counts, are reported as errors. Manual All Empty rooms to fill by hand. Elimination Two-team, BP Generated from the break; see Elimination draws . Two-team power pairing  Settings are on Configuration → Draw rules → Two-team bracket pairing and conflict avoidance : Odd bracket resolution method : pull a team up from the bracket below ( top , bottom , middle , random , or lowest draw-strength rank , the last two only with min-cost pairing with pull-ups), or form intermediate brackets ( intermediate , intermediate with bubble-up/bubble-down ; intermediate1 / intermediate2 for preallocated sides). Pull-up restriction can limit candidates to the least-pulled-up teams or the lowest draw strength. Pairing method within a bracket (ten-team examples): fold 1 v 10, slide 1 v 6, adjacent 1 v 2, random, or fold at the top and adjacent elsewhere. Conflict avoidance method : one-up-one-down (default; swaps second teams between adjacent rooms to remove clashes), minimum cost (exact minimum-weight matching per bracket over history, institution, side-balance, pull-up and pairing-deviation penalties), minimum cost with pull-ups (Tabbycat's single-graph matching over the whole field), or off . Sides , below. Team conflicts and clashes sets Avoid same institution , Avoid team history and their penalties. Pulled-up teams are marked on the debate and counted by the pullups standings metric. BP power pairing  Tabbycat's Hungarian BP draw ( Configuration → Draw rules → British Parliamentary (BP) draw rules ): brackets are completed to multiples of four from the bracket below, then one assignment of teams to (room, position) minimises position imbalance. BP pull-up distribution (anywhere, top or bottom rooms), BP position cost (Rényi entropy, variance or simple), Rényi order , BP position cost exponent and BP assignment method (shuffled Hungarian, unshuffled, or random within brackets) match Tabbycat's options. BP power pairing does not consider institution or history clashes, as in Tabbycat and the WUDC rules. Side allocation  Configuration → Draw rules → Side allocations and balancing → Side allocations method : Balanced (default): the team that has been affirmative more often goes negative; ties are decided by the seeded random source. Random. Preallocated (two-team): sides come from the Draw page (per round, or the all-rounds grid). Missing or uneven allocations are reported, not guessed. Chosen on the ballot (two-team; for example a coin toss): rooms are paired without sides; the draw, portals and printed ballots say "sides chosen at the debate", and the ballot records which team took which side. Confirming the ballot fixes the sides. Maximum allowed side imbalance (off by default) is a hard limit for every method: if neither side fits, the draw fails and names the room. Maximum number of times per side (default 5) only steers minimum-cost pairing and never blocks a draw; an excess shows as a warning in the draw check. Neither applies to BP. Elimination side rule  Sides in elimination rounds : By seed (default): the higher seed takes the first side (affirmative; in BP OG, OO, CG, CO by seed) and sides are final. Random, confirmed later (Tabbycat's behaviour): each room's teams are shuffled over its seats with the draw's seed and left unconfirmed. In two-team formats the ballot records which team took which side. BP ballots cannot record sides, so a BP room keeps its drawn seats, which you can swap in the editor. Byes  When the field cannot fill every room, Bye team selection method ( None , Lowest ranked or Random ) chooses who sits out; with None the draw needs a full field (or swing teams). Bye team results sets whether a bye is absent (no standings result) or a full win (two-team: a win; BP: 3 points and a first; N teams per room: 1 point). A bye never awards speaker scores, and speaker tabs and averages ignore it. Lowest-ranked ties are broken with the draw's seed. A swing team never takes a bye. Swing teams  When the available teams do not fill the last room, the Draw page's Swing teams panel says how many teams are short and offers a swing team instead of byes: give it a name and speakers (reserves, or registered speakers of other teams, who get separate speaker records so their own tab is unaffected). A swing team is available only in the rounds it is used in, is drawn like any team, never takes a bye, and its results count for its opponents. It and its speakers are left out of team standings, speaker and reply tabs and the break. Earlier swing teams can be reused in a later round. Elimination draws  Generate the break first (Results → Break ). Then, on the Draw page for the first elimination round, Generate draw builds a seeded bracket from the break. Break sizes that are not a full bracket start with a partial elimination : the top seeds advance directly and the rest are folded (best remaining seed against the weakest). BP eliminations work from any even field. Later rounds keep bracket positions, so teams stay in their half. Proceed to next round (Results) marks losing teams eliminated and activates the next elimination round. A round's elimination draw needs its break generated and every earlier elimination round of the category advanced. See Breaks and eliminations . N teams per room  For the N teams per room format (Tabbycat's Public Speaking preset uses 6): Random : the field is shuffled with the draw's seed and dealt into rooms of N; the last room holds the remainder (or the remainder gets byes with an automatic bye method). No conflict avoidance, history, institution or side rule applies. Manual : empty rooms of N positions ( Team 1 … Team N ); fill as many as a room needs, without gaps. Power-paired, seeded and round-robin draws, generated elimination draws, preallocated sides and sides chosen on the ballot are refused with a clear message, as in Tabbycat. Elimination rounds are added and drawn by hand. Regenerating a draw  No ballots yet: you confirm that the existing draw will be overwritten. The round has ballots: you are warned that regenerating will discard them; they stay in each ballot's history but no longer count. Only do this if the round was not debated as drawn. A confirmed or released draw, or one with a later round drawn after it, needs a recorded reason. A completed, cancelled or advanced round cannot be regenerated. Each generation creates debates with new ids, so old ballots never attach to new pairings. For cloud tournaments the replaced debates are soft-deleted live. Generating a preliminary draw while an earlier slot's round is unfinished needs a reason: unfinished results do not count towards power pairing. Reproducibility  Every random choice (shuffles, random pull-ups, tie-breaks, bye selection, random sides) uses one seeded random source. The seed is stored on the round and in the audit log, so the same inputs and seed reproduce the same draw, also in the background worker. Teams with equal standings, and teams with no standing yet, are ordered randomly with that seed. Differences from Tabbycat  Teams tied in a standings tier are ordered by the draw's seeded random order, not by database order (institution, then reference). In minimum-cost pairing, rematches are a weighted penalty, not forbidden, so a bracket where every option is a rematch still draws. Maximum allowed side imbalance (CrabbyTab's own) is a hard limit for every method; maximum times per side never blocks. Random side pre-allocation balances each team's affirmatives across rounds (Tabbycat shuffles each round independently). Elimination sides default to by seed ; Tabbycat's random, unconfirmed sides are an option. Swing teams are excluded from standings and the break automatically. Teams-only draw releases are not listed on the public draw page. N teams per room: a short last room is scored on its own teams; the anticipated draw gives rooms of more than 8 teams no bracket range. Limitations  One-up-one-down and intermediate with bubbles are local rules and may leave clashes that a different pairing would avoid. With one-up-one-down, pairing happens before sides are known; if two teams cannot take opposite sides within the side-imbalance limit, the bracket is re-paired, and if that fails the draw stops with an error naming them. BP and minimum-cost pairing are O(n³); they run in a Web Worker, so a 1000-team round takes a few seconds without freezing the page. Divisions only restrict which teams a round draws; there are no per-division standings.

Adjudicator allocation and preformed panels  The Allocation page (sidebar → Round · R1 → Allocation , administrators and staff with the allocation permission) assigns adjudicators to the round's debates automatically and lets you adjust panels by hand. Assignments stay private until you reveal them. Exact formulas: docs/adjudicator-allocation.md . Allocation is a heuristic : it finds a good allocation, not a proven optimum. Step by step  Check adjudicator availability on the round's Availability page ( how ). On the Allocation page, choose the round and, under Allocation engine , the panel sizing ( Same size everywhere with a Panel size , or Larger in priority rooms with a Largest panel ) and the round's Feedback weight (%) . Optionally set room importance: per debate (0–10), or for every room with Prioritise by bracket or Prioritise by liveness (below). Press Auto-Allocate All . Warnings (clashes, rooms short of adjudicators, unavailable preformed-panel members) are listed under Allocated with warnings . Adjust by hand. Clashes show on each panel. Allocate rooms on the Draw page ( Allocate venues ) if you have not yet; see Venues and constraints . Release the draw, then press Reveal Adjudicators so teams and the public see the panels (after the release uploads). Other controls: Clear Allocations (with confirmation), Priority Info (each debate's priority and panel strength), Diversity (gender and region badges and a per-panel summary), Shards (below), and the Preformed panels link. Who is allocated  Adjudicators available for the round, unless Skip adjudicator check-ins is on. Adjudicators busy in a concurrent round are left out. Adjudicators scoring below Minimum adjudicator score to vote (default 1.5) are placed as trainees, never left out, as in Tabbycat. Trainees are seated after the voting panels unless No trainee adjudicators is on; No panellist adjudicators allocates chairs (and trainees) only. With either switch on, the editor hides and refuses that position. Auto-allocation is refused, leaving existing panels untouched, when no adjudicator is available or none may vote. Allocating a draft draw is allowed. Re-allocating a draw already released, or a round with live ballots or that is completed, needs a recorded reason. These switches and the penalties below are on Admin → Configuration → Draw rules → Adjudicator allocation and panel rules . Adjudicator scores  Pre-feedback score: the test score if set, otherwise the base score (1–10). Feedback average: weighted average of counted feedback (confirmed and not ignored), mapped from the feedback scale onto 1–10. Weights come from Feedback weighting by source on the Feedback page. Blended score: (1 − w) × pre-feedback + w × feedback average , where w is the round's feedback weight . Adjudicators without counted feedback keep their pre-feedback score. New rounds start with feedback weight 100% , so once an adjudicator has counted feedback it replaces their base or test score. Lower the weight if base scores should keep influence. A round without a weight blends at 60% (CrabbyTab's strategies) or uses the base score (Tabbycat strategies). Debate priority and liveness  CrabbyTab's own strategy ranks debates by a blend of the bracket (40%), break liveness (40%) and the manual importance (20%), then, with less weight, room priority. Liveness follows Tabbycat: per break category, a team is live , safe or dead from the completed rounds. It shows in standings, on the Draw page ( Live teams: N per room) and on the Allocation page ( N% live per debate). Two buttons set every room's importance at once (replacing importances already set in the round): Prioritise by bracket : splits the rooms into quarters by bracket and sets importance 10, 7, 3 and 0, highest brackets first. Prioritise by liveness : uses the general break's live thresholds before the round: rooms where every team is safe get 7, rooms where every team is dead get 0, every other room 10. Available in preliminary rounds with a general break category of more than one team. Allocation strategies  Configuration → Draw rules → Adjudicator allocation strategy : Strategy Behaviour Preset 1 — Current CrabbyTab allocation ( crabbytab_v1 , default) Seat ranks matched to adjudicator ranks by priority; panel size from the Allocation page. Panel average ( panel_average ) As Preset 1, but each panel's average strength is matched to the debate priority. Tabbycat voting ( tabbycat_voting ) Port of Tabbycat's hungarian-voting : the strongest adjudicators chair the most important rooms alone; the rest form panels of three. Ignores panel size. Tabbycat consensus ( tabbycat_consensus ) Port of Tabbycat's hungarian-consensus : every voter is spread as evenly as possible; the most important rooms get the extra member. Ignores panel size. The Tabbycat ports use Tabbycat's cost function, its 0–5 score scale (mapped from CrabbyTab's 1–10) and each debate's own importance; debates are taken by importance, then room rank. Tabbycat itself always uses its voting allocator for per-adjudicator ballots and its consensus allocator otherwise; in CrabbyTab you choose. How CrabbyTab's own strategies work  Preformed panels are placed first (below). Panel sizes: Same size everywhere gives every debate the chosen size, dropping seats from the lowest-priority debates when adjudicators run out; Larger in priority rooms gives every debate a chair, then grows panels to 3, 5, … in priority order. A Hungarian assignment fills the seats, with costs for strength mismatch ( Importance mismatch penalty ), team conflicts ( Adjudicator conflict penalty ) and teams already judged ( Adjudicator history penalty , soft). A local search reduces adjudicator–adjudicator conflicts and repeated co-panelling (bounded so large tournaments stay responsive). Trainees go, lowest-scored first, to the debate with the lowest conflict cost, then fewest trainees, then lowest priority. The strongest panel member without a team clash becomes chair . With the default penalties (conflict 1,000,000, history 10,000, mismatch 10,000,000), one conflict always costs more than any strength mismatch, and a one-point mismatch more than one repeat. Penalties are used exactly as configured: a low conflict penalty can let a conflict through (it is reported), and 0 turns that check off. Every remaining clash is listed on the result and in the audit log. Allocation runs in a background worker; a Cancel button stops a long run and saves nothing. Conflicts  Conflicts are edited in the adjudicator dialog (Setup → Adjudicators : Team conflicts , Adjudicator conflicts , Other institution conflicts ) and on Setup → Conflicts (CSV import, team–institution conflicts, full list). An adjudicator clashes with a team when: institutional : the adjudicator's own institution (unless independent) or a declared institution matches the team's institution, a composite team's other institutions, or an institution the team declared a conflict with; personal : the adjudicator declared a conflict with that team; history (soft): the adjudicator has judged the team before. Two adjudicators clash when either declared a personal conflict with the other, or they share a conflicted institution. Clashes are shown on the panel ("Institutional", "Personal", "Adjudicator", "History") and in the draw check. Conflicts are never shown publicly. See Participants and imports . Editing panels by hand  Drag judges from Available Adjudicators (searchable by name or institution) onto a chair, panellist or trainee slot, or use the keyboard and touch equivalent: Move picks a judge, then each debate offers Place as chair ( Replace chair when one is set; the old chair returns to the pool), Add as panellist and Add as trainee , or Return to pool . Arrow keys, Home and End move between targets; Escape cancels. A clash preview shows while a judge is picked, and refusals (for example a trainee dropped on a chair slot) are announced. Changing a panel after Reveal Adjudicators hides the adjudicators again; reveal once you are done. For cloud tournaments, panels are written live: another administrator device sees each change within seconds. Two devices editing the same panel: the last full panel written wins (panels are never mixed). Shards  For large rounds, Shards splits the board into 2–6 parts to work on: sort by Bracket , Priority or Venue , and mix Top to bottom or Interleaved . A shard is only a view: auto-allocation and the conflict checks always cover the whole round. Preformed panels  Preformed panels let the adjudication core build panels before the draw exists ( Preformed panels link on the Allocation page, /{slug}/allocation/panels ). Turn on Allocate preformed panels as a unit (Configuration → Draw rules); otherwise auto-allocation ignores the panels. Pick the round and create panels: Add panel , Create from CSV panel ids (from the adjudicator import's preformed_panel_id ), or Create from anticipated draw : one panel per room the next draw is expected to have, annotated with its possible bracket range and how many teams may still be live (Tabbycat's anticipated draw). Set importance: by hand (0–10), Prioritise by bracket or Prioritise by liveness (live panels 10, safe 7, the rest 0). Fill members by hand, or Auto-allocate adjudicators (Tabbycat's voting or consensus allocator over the panels, replacing members). Review, then Save panels . When allocating, Placing preformed panels decides how panels reach debates: Optimised (importance, conflicts, history) (default): Tabbycat's Hungarian preformed-panel allocator. A panel goes where its importance matches the debate's importance, with team conflicts and history added as costs. By room rank (no optimisation) : Tabbycat's direct allocator: the panel with the lowest room rank goes to the debate with the lowest room rank, and so on. Members unavailable this round are left out and named in the warnings; a panel with no available voting member is not placed. Debates without a panel are then filled by the normal allocator. Testers  An adjudicator can be marked Tester (adjudicator dialog, or the Tester column on the feedback overview); members of the adjudication core always are. An adjudicator counts as tested in a round when another tester sat on their panel; the adjudicator record marks those rounds "Tested". See Feedback . Differences from Tabbycat  CrabbyTab allows allocating a draft draw (its draws can be released straight from draft); Tabbycat requires a confirmed draw. Re-allocating a released draw needs a reason instead of being refused. The Tabbycat strategies do not shuffle voters (ties break by score, then id, so results are reproducible) and use a symmetric judged-together history. CrabbyTab's own strategies seat every trainee; Tabbycat's voting allocator may leave surplus trainees out. In optimised preformed-panel placement, debates without a panel are filled by the normal allocator (Tabbycat clears them). Limitations  Diversity (gender, region) is shown, but is not an allocation constraint. The Hungarian matching is O(n³); with ~1000 seats it takes a second or more, much longer when every adjudicator has the same score. It runs in a Web Worker, so the page stays usable.

Venues and constraints  Rooms ("venues") are managed on Setup → Venues ; soft room preferences on Setup → Room preferences . Rooms are allocated after the draw from the Draw page, and again after adjudicator allocation when adjudicators have room needs. Venues  A venue has: Field Meaning Room name Shown in the draw, portals and emails Priority rank Higher = better room, used for top-bracket and important debates (default 10 on import) Category One or more room categories, comma-separated (e.g. "Large, Accessible") Capacity (seats) Optional; blank means no limit Accessible , Online-capable , near tab room Capabilities matched against requirements. Near tab room is set through the CSV near_tab_room column (not in the dialog). Room link Optional http(s) map or meeting link, shown in the draw, private URLs, public draw data and emails ( {{venue_url}} ) Availability The room's default availability, and an override per round Add venue adds one; Import CSV imports many at once (columns name , priority , category / categories , capacity , accessible , online , near_tab_room , url ; see CSV formats ). The venue CSV imports directly, without a preview. Availability  A room is used in a round when it is available : its per-round setting (the In {round} toggle on the Venues page) if set, otherwise its default. An unavailable room is never allocated. Rooms used by a concurrent round in the same schedule slot are never offered either. Rooms can also be checked in on the round's Availability page (tick, or barcode). The check-in is informational: it records a time, and with Room check-in expiry (Configuration → Public visibility) old check-ins show as Expired . Allocation uses availability, not check-in. Room categories  The Room categories card on the Venues page describes each category (the text follows "This room …" in tooltips; shown on public pages only when ticked) and whether its name is shown as a prefix or suffix of room names. Requirements, preferences and filters match any of a room's categories. Hard requirements  Requirements must hold; a debate is never put in an unsuitable room. They can be set on: debates — on the Draw page room card: Required category , Minimum seats , Accessible , Online-capable , Near tab room ; teams, adjudicators and institutions — through the CSV import columns required_venue_category , min_venue_capacity , requires_accessible_venue , requires_online_venue , requires_near_tab_room (or the API). When a draw is generated, the requirements of the debate's teams and their institutions are combined: the largest capacity wins and the flags add up. Two different required categories among a debate's teams is an error ("Teams in a debate require incompatible venue categories"). Adjudicator requirements are added when adjudicators are allocated; if a panel's adjudicators need different categories, the debate keeps its own category and the conflict is reported instead of stopping the allocation. Soft room preferences  Setup → Room preferences (Tabbycat's venue constraints): a team, adjudicator or institution prefers rooms of a category , with a whole-number priority . Add them one at a time ( Add preference ) or import a CSV (one row per preference: team , adjudicator or institution , plus category and priority ; preview first). Allocation meets them where it can: missing one preference of a priority costs more than missing every lower-priority one together, any preference outweighs room ranking, and none is ever met at the cost of a hard requirement. Unmet preferences appear as warnings in the draw check. Allocating rooms  On the Draw page, Allocate venues assigns compatible available rooms by debate priority. Rooms are also allocated when a draw is generated, and again after auto-allocating adjudicators when any adjudicator has room requirements or preferences. The allocator finds a minimum-cost assignment (CrabbyTab finds the best assignment where Tabbycat assigns greedily, debate by debate): Hard requirements must hold. Room preferences are met where possible, by priority. Higher-ranked debates (bracket, importance) get higher-priority rooms. Byes and postponed debates get no room. Too few rooms never stops a draw (as Tabbycat's room allocator): as many debates as possible get a room, the lowest-ranked go without, the Draw page says so before generating ("Only X venues are available for Y rooms…"), and the draw check lists every debate without a room. Messages are explicit: Not enough available venues: X required, but only Y available, so {room} has no room. No available venue meets the requirements for {room}. Available venues cannot satisfy all debate requirements at the same time, so {room} has no room. Add or enable rooms, then press Allocate venues again. Assigning by hand  Choose a room from the venue menu on a room card. Rooms that are unavailable in this round, already used by another debate, or that do not meet the debate's requirements are refused with the reason. An existing mismatch is shown on the card ( Assigned venue does not meet requirements: … ). Changing rooms after the draw is released needs no override. Details  Room changes (venues, categories, availability, preferences) are saved on this device and reach other devices and the public pages with Upload now . A debate's assigned room is part of the draw, which is live on administrator devices. Availability of every room in every round is in Admin → Data exports → Availability . Logic: src/lib/draw/venueAllocator.ts , src/lib/venues/ . Developer details: docs/adjudicator-allocation.md (section "Rooms"). Limitations  Team, adjudicator and institution requirements can only be set by CSV (or the API), not in the participant dialogs. There are no room constraints by time slot beyond concurrent rounds.

x: Ballots and results  Results are entered as ballots . A debate can have several ballot versions ; the one confirmed, non-discarded version is the result. Standings are calculated live from confirmed ballots. Where things are: Task Where Enter, check and confirm ballots Sidebar Results → Results (page Results & ballot entry ): pick the round, then Enter ballot / Edit ballot on a debate Print ballot sheets, scan paper ballots Print ballot sheets and Ballot intake links on the Results page (see Printing and display ) Ballot settings Admin → Configuration → Scoring & ballots , card Ballot rules and options Private-URL ballots, individual ballots, self-split Admin → Assistants (page Tournament access ), card Staff access and private-URL ballots Public (non-private-URL) ballot form Same page, card Public forms (see Public pages and releases ) Motion preferences Setup → Motions , card Motion settings Deep reference: results-and-ballots.md , ballot-intake.md , staff-access.md . Ballot settings  All on Configuration → Scoring & ballots unless stated. Setting Default What it does Minimum / maximum speaker score, score step; reply minimum / maximum format preset Range and step every speech is checked against Ballot introduction/explanation empty Text shown on the tab-room ballot page, printed ballots, private-URL and public ballot forms Margin includes dissenters off Voting ballots: scores, totals and margins come from the whole panel instead of the majority Team score includes ghosts on for new tournaments Iron-person (ghost) speeches count towards the team total Require double-entry ballot verification off A second person must check each tab-room ballot (see below) How ballots are checked Review Review or Blind double entry Ballots per debate, preliminary rounds Consensus Consensus (one ballot per panel) or Voting (one sheet per voting adjudicator). Two-team formats only; BP is always consensus Ballots per debate, elimination rounds Same as preliminary Locked once an elimination ballot exists Record motion vetoes format preset Each team may record the motion it vetoed Allow forfeits off Two-team only: record a debate as forfeited by one side Allow motion reuse on Reuse a motion in another round Deciding the winner from the scores See Deciding the winner Ballots ask for speaker scores Always Always , Preliminary rounds only or Never ( results-only ballots ) Speech ranks Do not rank Consensus ballots rank every substantive speech (adds the Speech ranks (sum) speaker metric) Panel score aggregation (voting ballots) Mean Mean or Median Maximum margin 0 (no limit) Two-team: no scoresheet may have a bigger margin Reply score step half the speaker step Step for reply scores Reply speaker must have given a substantive speech on The last substantive speaker can never reply either way Side names Affirmative/Negative Two-team formats: Government/Opposition, Proposition/Opposition, Pro/Con, Team 1/Team 2 and others; used everywhere sides are shown Record motions on ballots on Off: ballots and printed scoresheets do not ask for the motion or vetoes Score criteria none Weighted criteria (e.g. WSDC Style/Content/Strategy); a speech's score is the weighted sum Bye team results ( Draw rules ) Absent Win gives a bye team a win (see Byes ) Locked once ballots exist: the format, teams per debate, substantive speakers, reply scoring, preliminary ballot mode, Ballots ask for speaker scores and score criteria (existing ballots would no longer fit). Changing a scoring setting after ballots exist asks for confirmation; see Recalculating stored ballots . Consensus and voting ballots  Consensus Voting Formats All Two-team formats, and N-team rooms ( see below ); never BP Sheets One ballot for the whole panel One scoresheet per voting adjudicator: chair and panellists; trainees never vote Winner From the scores / declared, per Deciding the winner Each sheet votes; the majority wins Speaker scores As entered Combined per speech over the relevant sheets (majority, or the whole panel with Margin includes dissenters ) Team totals and margin Own total − opponent total (two-team); BP has no margin Mean of the relevant sheets' own totals and margins Points. BP: 1st = 3, 2nd = 2, 3rd = 1, 4th = 0. Two-team: win = 1. N-team rooms: teams in the room − rank. Preliminary round points are multiplied by the round's weight ( Round settings ); wins and speaks are not. Voting ballots in practice Allocate a chair (the page says Allocate a chair before entering voting ballots ). The speaker order is set on the chair's sheet and shared by every sheet. Enter each adjudicator's scores. Every sheet must produce a winner. A tied panel (e.g. 1–1) is decided by the chair's sheet. With no chair sheet the ballot is refused. Fill from private-URL ballots copies each adjudicator's latest private-URL sheet into the ballot and warns about disagreements and missing adjudicators. Mean or median. Mean is exact (not rounded). Median follows Tabbycat: an odd panel takes the median; an even panel takes the mean rounded up to a whole number (75 and 76 give 76). With score criteria each criterion is combined separately. Team totals and margins are always the mean of the sheets' totals. Deciding the winner  Option Two-team BP From the scores (default) Higher total wins; tied totals invalid Ranks follow totals; tied totals invalid Declared, as a check Declared winner must have the higher total As "from the scores" Declared, to break ties Equal totals allowed; declared winner may not have the lower total Entered ranks may order teams with equal totals Declared, overriding the scores Low-point wins allowed Any ranks accepted This replaces the old Allow low-point wins switch (still read for older tournaments). It applies to every voting sheet as well. Validation  A ballot is checked before it saves; the page lists every problem. Speeches: exactly the configured number of substantive speeches per team, in order, by speakers on the team's roster. Scores: within range and on the step (or each criterion within its own range and step). Ranks / winner: see above. BP needs each rank 1st–4th once. Maximum margin , when set. Replies (two-team, reply scoring on): one per team, not by the last substantive speaker, and (by default) by someone who gave a counted substantive speech. Speech ranks , when on: no ties; with "ranks must follow the scores", a higher score may not be ranked below a lower one. Motion and vetoes: the motion must be one of the round's motions; a veto must be another of the round's motions. Iron-person (ghost) speeches  If a speaker appears twice the ballot is refused until the extra speech is marked Ghost (the button next to the speech). Ghost speeches never count in the speaker tab; they count towards the team total only with Team score includes ghosts . Self-split ballots  Allow self-split ballots for solo adjudicators (Assistants page, Tabbycat's Karl Popper rule). In a two-team voting round, when a debate has exactly one voting adjudicator, the ballot page shows This was a 2:1 split decision (self-declared) . The winner is recorded with 2 votes and the loser 1, out of 3. Scores, winner and margin do not change. In standings the votes/ballots carried metric credits 2/3 and 1/3 of a panel. With Show splitting adjudicators on, the public site marks the adjudicator as splitting. Refused when the setting is off, the panel has more than one voting adjudicator, or the round uses consensus ballots. The checkbox is also on that adjudicator's private-URL ballot. Turning the setting off does not change saved ballots. Motions, vetoes and preferences on ballots  Motion debated. With one motion in the round it is recorded automatically. With several, the ballot asks which was debated; private-URL and public-form ballots must answer (checked on the server, never defaulted). Vetoes ( Record motion vetoes ): one optional veto per team, from the round's other motions. Also offered on private-URL and public-form ballots. Vetoes appear in the motion statistics on Analytics , and publicly only once the veto statistics are released (see Public pages and releases ). Versions, confirming and discarding  Every save is a new version . The Ballot versions list on the entry page shows each with its status ( Confirmed , Discarded , Awaiting check ), the submitter ( Tab room , Public form , Adjudicator (private URL) ) and time, with Edit as new version , Confirm vN and Discard vN . Confirming a version unconfirms the previously confirmed one; drafts and other versions are left as they are (Tabbycat's behaviour). It writes the points and totals onto the debate and records who confirmed it. A ballot whose teams no longer match the current draw cannot be confirmed (protects regenerated draws). A confirmed or discarded version is never edited in place: corrections are saved as a new version. An unconfirmed new version leaves the existing confirmed result in force until it is confirmed. Discarding the confirmed version clears the result (you are warned). The debate goes back to draft if other versions remain, else none . Confirming or discarding a result withdraws the round's published results and team speaks so nothing stale stays public. Publish again when ready. Changing a result in a completed round asks for confirmation; results of an elimination round whose teams have advanced, or of a cancelled round, cannot change. Two devices. On cloud tournaments, ballots of the active round sync live between administrator devices. A different person sees Version N, entered by …, is waiting for your check , compares it with the paper and confirms or discards it. If they change anything they can only Save corrected version (needs another check) . Blind: the checker re-enters the paper ballot without seeing the first entry (its scores are Hidden during blind check in the history). Matching entries confirm the result and the checked entry is discarded. If they differ, The two entries do not match lists the differences (motion, forfeit, vetoes, sides, ranks/winners, self-split, every speech, or every sheet) and lets the checker record either entry; the other is kept as a discarded version. Byes count only when Bye team results (Configuration → Draw rules) is Award a win (no speaker scores) . A bye win is worth 1 point in every format (in BP that is a 3rd place), with no speaker scores or margin, as in Tabbycat. BP records no wins. Round weights (Configuration → Round settings → Points weight by round ) multiply the team points earned in that round. Wins and who-beat-whom are not weighted. Forfeits and results-only ballots count for the result but not for speaker scores or margins. Ghost (iron-person) speeches never count on the speaker tab. A drawn debate whose result is not confirmed yet still counts for draw strength and pull-ups , as Tabbycat counts every preliminary debate for those; it adds nothing else. Swing teams are not ranked (their results still count for their opponents). This is a deliberate difference from Tabbycat. The admin Standings page is live : it uses every confirmed ballot as soon as it is confirmed, without waiting for the round to be completed. Public tabs are different: they use completed preliminary rounds only and appear only once released (see Public pages and releases ). Missing data is "no value", not zero  A metric with no data has no value , shown as "—", not 0. This follows Tabbycat, where sums, averages and standard deviations over no results are NULL , while counts are 0. A team with no confirmed results yet has no points, speaker scores or margins, but 0 wins. A speaker with no speeches has no total, average, standard deviation, trimmed mean or speech-rank sum, but 0 speeches. No value ranks below every value , whichever direction the metric ranks in, and teams with no value tie with each other. So a standard deviation of 0 is the best value, but a team with no scores ranks last on it. Power-pairing brackets read "no value" as 0, as Tabbycat's draw does. Break liveness  Before each preliminary round CrabbyTab computes Tabbycat's live / safe / dead thresholds for every break category, from points earned in earlier preliminary rounds: Safe : at or above the safe score (certain to break). Dead : at or below the dead score (cannot break). Live : in between. A general category's thresholds come from the number of non-swing teams, rounds and break size. Other categories also use their own teams' points. A category with a break of one team or less has no status; one with no more teams than its break makes everyone safe. These are strict mathematical bounds, as in Tabbycat: they ignore institution caps, overrides and teams breaking in a higher-priority category. Treat them as a guide. Points are raw (not multiplied by round weights), as in Tabbycat. Where it shows, as text badges such as "Open: live": Standings → Teams : a Break liveness column for the next preliminary round that is not completed (hidden once all are completed, and when viewing standings as of a round). Draw page (preliminary rounds): each team's status per category, and each room's number of live team-category pairs. Allocation page → Prioritise debates → By liveness : sets room importance from the general category's thresholds (safe-only rooms 7, dead-only rooms 0, others 10). See Adjudicator allocation . Analytics  Results → Analytics shows: ballot completion per round; a speaker score histogram over confirmed ballots (fixed 68–84 bins; scores are rounded and scores outside the range are not shown); side balance: average points and wins (1sts in BP) per side or position; motion balance per motion and round: debates, wins per side, vetoes when recorded, and a χ² p-value with a low expected count warning. Not shown for N-teams-per-room formats. Details  Speaker categories. Filtering speakers uses speaker category ids (older label data resolves by name). On the public site, each public speaker category gets its own released tab, cut at the category's limit; private category membership is never published. Draw strength by rank is the mean standings rank of a team's opponents; it is computed from the ranking, so it can only be an extra column. Tabbycat differences: null values rank last in every precedence (Tabbycat's Python sort path, used with who-beat-whom, draw strength or speaks_ind_avg , counts them as 0); swing teams are not ranked; tied teams in a draw bracket are ordered by the draw's seeded random order rather than database order. See Comparison with Tabbycat . Changed behaviour from early versions: the trimmed mean now drops from both ends (default 1); BP byes are 1 point and a 3rd, not 3 points; BP no longer counts 1st/2nd as wins; Times pulled up ranks more as higher.

Institution rank (the AIDA rules' "nth team of its institution") is counted over every team in the category's standings, including ineligible, excluded and already-broken teams, and teams tied in the standings share it. Institutions are matched by id, falling back to the name. Ranking within a category  A general category ranks every team on the overall standings and keeps overall ranks (column "Tab rank"). A non-general category ranks only its own teams (eligible plus manually included) among themselves: ranks restart at 1 (column "Category rank") and who-beat-whom compares teams tied within the category. Teams that broke in a higher-priority category stay in this ranking, so the first ESL breaker can be ranked 2nd. Other metrics (draw strength included) are tournament-wide values. Overrides  Under Manual overrides , each team can get one override per category: Manually included : takes a break place first, bypassing eligibility and caps. A team still never breaks in two categories of different priority. Ineligible , Withdrawn , Different break , Disqualified , Lost coin toss : remove the team from this category. The list of excluded teams shows every manual exclusion, plus rule-based exclusions (different break, capped) of teams ranked above the last breaking team. Overrides (remarks) are never published. Ties at the cutoff  When teams level on every precedence metric straddle the last breaking place or the last reserve place, CrabbyTab holds the whole tied group out and refuses to generate the break until you decide. It never settles a tie by name or any other arbitrary order, and never makes a break larger than its size (the elimination bracket depends on it). The Break page lists the tied teams as "Tied" and explains the fix; Generate Break stays disabled. Resolve it (for example by coin toss) with overrides: Manually included for the team(s) that go through (the others stay in the running for reserve places), or Lost coin toss for the others. Reserve places after a tied group are counted from the end of the group, as Tabbycat does: a break of 3 + 2 reserves with three teams tied for 2 places leaves one reserve place. This differs from Tabbycat, which lets every tied team through and leaves it to the tab director. Break ranks. The Seed column shows each breaking team's break rank as Tabbycat does: teams tied on every metric (for example two manually included teams) share it, shown as "=2". The bracket still uses a unique seed per team. Reserves show R1, R2, …. Generating the break  Generate Break (or Regenerate Break ) for one category: is refused (hard rules) when there are too few eligible teams for the break size, when a cutoff tie is unresolved, or when an elimination round the change would touch has already been drawn or advanced; warns (a soft rule you can override with a recorded reason) when preliminary rounds are not finished; needs a valid break size and enough pre-created, non-cancelled elimination rounds; assigns categories to elimination rounds by schedule: smaller breaks join later rounds (with N teams per room, every category is in every elimination round); marks this category's teams breaking (teams that break in no category become eliminated ); other categories keep their own generated break; stores a snapshot of the break and writes an audit event, then makes the category's first elimination round the active round. If standings, settings or overrides change afterwards, the page warns that the calculated break differs from the generated one; regenerate to apply it. A generated break can also be cleared through the API (refused once one of its rounds has a draw); see API and tokens . The break is not public until you release that category in the Public release panel on the Standings page; see Public pages and releases . Elimination draws  Draw the elimination round on the Draw page as usual (see Rounds and draws ). Seeds are the teams' places in the category's break; each team keeps its bracket position throughout. Bracket positions carry forward : later rounds inherit the position of the room a team came from instead of re-seeding. Full fields (two-team 2ᵏ, BP 4 × 2ᵏ) use standard seeded brackets, e.g. two-team 16: 1v16, 8v9, 4v13, 5v12, 2v15, 7v10, 3v14, 6v11; BP 16: [1,8,9,16], [4,5,12,13], [2,7,10,15], [3,6,11,14]. Sides follow Configuration → Draw rules → Sides in elimination rounds : By seed (default; the higher seed takes Affirmative / Opening Government and sides are final) or Random (as Tabbycat; drawn with the draw's seed and left unconfirmed, and two-team ballots record the sides taken). N teams per room : elimination draws are not generated (as in Tabbycat). Set the round's draw type to manual and draw it by hand. Partial eliminations  A break that does not halve cleanly (e.g. 12 two-team teams, or 24 or 6 BP teams) starts with a partial elimination round . With T the largest full field below N, the top 2T − N seeds get an elimination bye (they advance without a ballot), and the remaining seeds are folded: two-team, best remaining against weakest; BP room j holds seeds B+j, T+1−j, T+j, N+1−j. The Break page shows "Partial elimination: the top N seeds get a bye". Advancing  When every non-bye debate has a confirmed ballot, press Proceed to next round on the Results page of the elimination round. It: checks the round has a draw, every eligible team is in a debate, no team that did not qualify for this stage is in the round, and every ballot names the draw's current teams; advances the winner (two-team), the top two of each room (BP; the winner only in the final), or for N teams per room the top two by rank (one in the final) or the teams a results-only ballot declares advancing; marks the rest eliminated, marks the round completed, and activates the next elimination round. Elimination rounds never count in standings. Breaking adjudicators  Breaking adjudicators ( /break/adjudicators ) lists every adjudicator with a search, a Breaking only filter and an inline breaking toggle (also available from the feedback overview). There is no adjudicator break calculation; releasing the public list is a separate switch in the Public release panel. Details and differences from Tabbycat  Cutoff ties are held out for the tab director instead of all breaking. Swing teams never break and are left out of liveness counts. Elimination sides default to By seed (Tabbycat randomises); choose Random to match Tabbycat. BP eliminations work from any even field of at least 4 teams, using partial elimination rounds. WADL is not a Tabbycat break rule and is not offered. Break liveness (safe / live / dead) is described on Standings and metrics .

The rest of this page covers what each release shows and where you switch it. How publishing works  Public pages never read your live data. They show a cleaned-up public snapshot of the cloud copy, built by the server when you publish. A value that is hidden is left out of the snapshot, so it is not just hidden on the page. Open public pages check for a new version every 45 seconds. Releases publish in one step. Release buttons open a dialog that saves the change, uploads this device's other pending changes and publishes the public pages. The dialog tells you how many other changes go up with it. If the upload or publish fails, it says the change is saved on this device but not public yet . This applies to: draw stages, round results, team speaks, motion releases, the schedule, and every item on the Public release panel. A release is refused while you are offline or while records conflict with the cloud (resolve those first). On a device without cloud sync, the change is saved on that device only. If this device has changes that are not uploaded, it asks first ( Upload and publish , or Publish cloud copy anyway ). An upload that hit conflicts, or that stopped part-way, does not update public pages. The top bar says so and shows how to recover. (The page has no button to change one participant's passcode.) A speaker's link opens only their own team, and only with that speaker's passcode. A removed speaker's link opens nothing. Keys and passcodes are visible to administrators only. Data-entry staff never receive them, and they are never published or returned by the REST API. The REST API's /me endpoints accept the same key and passcode, so participants can use apps built on it ( API and tokens ). Differences from Tabbycat  Speaker links are optional; Tabbycat gives every speaker one. Team links remain the default. Private URLs and public forms are separate switches. In Tabbycat "private URLs" and "public" are exclusive choices. Portal check-in, ballots and feedback reach the tab room through the cloud copy, not instantly. Details  A portal load reads only the participant's own debates (through a participant index), their teams and ballots, and the rounds. Rounds are sent with a whitelist of fields, so preformed panels, pre-allocated sides and draw seeds never reach participants. The adjudicator portal shows the debate's motion as soon as the draw is released, without waiting for the motion release. In rounds with several motions, it also receives the round's motions so the ballot can ask which was debated. Developer detail: public-pages-and-notifications.md (speaker private URLs, QR slips, self check-in), results-and-ballots.md , staff-access.md .

Email and notifications  The Email page (sidebar → Public → Email, administrators only; titled Tournament email ) sends plain-text email through your SMTP server, sends automatic notifications, holds the tournament's email templates and keeps a history. Everything is sent by the server; nothing is sent from the browser. Setting up SMTP  SMTP is configured by whoever deploys CrabbyTab, as server environment variables ( SMTP_HOST , SMTP_PORT (default 587), SMTP_SECURE , SMTP_USER , SMTP_PASS , SMTP_FROM ), plus FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON ; see Installation . Credentials are never stored in tournament data. Port 587 uses STARTTLS, port 465 implicit TLS. Use Send test email on the Email page to check the setup. Without SMTP every send fails before anything is recorded as sent. Sending an email by hand  Under Compose tournament email , pick Recipients : Group Who All teams / Breaking teams / Non-breaking teams Every speaker with an email on those teams All adjudicators / Checked-in adjudicators / All trainees Adjudicators with an email All participants Teams and adjudicators Teams in a round / Adjudicators in a round / Chairs in a round / Panellists in a round Needs a Round Institution coaches and representatives Coaches stored on institutions (registration representatives once saved as coaches) Pick a Template : Tournament announcement, Round details, Adjudicator assignment, Feedback reminder, Adjudicator private portal credentials, Team private portal credentials, or Custom. The two credential templates also switch the recipients to all adjudicators / all teams. Saved templates from Email settings and templates can be loaded with Use in the compose form (see below). Edit subject and message, check the preview, tick the confirmation and send. Each recipient gets a separate message. Addresses are de-duplicated (case-insensitive). Limits: at most 100 unique recipients per send , subject up to 200 characters on one line, message up to 20,000 characters. Variables  Write {{variable}} (spaces inside the braces are allowed). An unknown variable is an error. Variables Filled with name email tournament round institution team Always available ( team empty for adjudicators) long_name The team's long name with institution (Tabbycat LONG) debate venue venue_url chair panellists position The recipient's debate in the chosen round; position is Chair, Panellist or Trainee private_url passcode key The recipient's private portal link, passcode, and link key speakers code_name emoji break_categories Team registration details (empty for adjudicators) side result points ballot motions Filled only in the matching automatic notifications entry url teams_allocated adjudicators_allocated Filled only in registration emails Private links: If the template uses {{private_url}} or {{passcode}} and a recipient has none, the send is refused ("Generate private URLs and try again"). A send is refused if one address would receive two different private links (for example a speaker on two teams). Speakers get their team's link, or their own speaker link if they have one. Coaches have no private link. History and retries  Campaign history lists the latest 50 sends (manual, retries and automatic notifications) with status, sender, counts and per-recipient errors. Retry failed resends only to failed recipients; each attempt can be retried once (retry the latest attempt after that). Private links and passcodes are never stored in the history; a retry looks them up again. Automatic notifications  Turn each event on in Automatic notifications on the Email page. All are off by default. Event Sent to When Draw released Each team's speakers The draw is released to teams (teams-only or full release) Draw released Each adjudicator on a panel The draw is fully released and panels are revealed Team results Each team's speakers (result and running team points) The round's results are released, the round is not silent and public results are on Motions released Speakers and adjudicators in the round (motions and info slides) Motions released and the draw fully released Ballot confirmed Consensus: every adjudicator of the debate, trainees included. Never for BP elimination rounds How they work: The server reads the cloud copy : a release is emailed only after it has been uploaded . Each upload sends what is due; Send due notifications now does the same on demand. Turning an event on marks items already released in the cloud as done, so old rounds are not emailed (the message says how many were skipped). Each event and round is sent once, in chunks of up to 100 recipients claimed in a transaction first, so concurrent triggers never double-send. A claimed chunk that fails is not resent automatically: use Retry failed . Team results count released, non-silent preliminary rounds only. A team without a confirmed result gets no email (never a zero). Elimination rounds produce no team-results email. Ballot confirmed only covers running rounds (draw out, not completed); confirmations in completed rounds are not emailed. A failing receipt never fails the ballot submission. Email settings and templates  Email settings and templates (Email page) is stored on the server and applies to the next email at once (no upload needed): Setting Effect Reply-To name / address Added to every email the tournament sends: campaigns, retries, notifications, receipts, registration emails Email registrants Sends Registration received and Registration approved to registrants Templates Your own subject and message for each event below; Reset this template to the default undoes it. Unknown variables are refused on save Templates: Draw released (teams), Draw released (adjudicators), Team results, Ballot receipt, Ballot confirmed, Motions released, Private URL, Feedback URL, Team registration details, Registration received, Registration approved, Places allocated, Institution registered. Private URL , Feedback URL and Team registration details are sent by hand: Use in the compose form loads them (Team registration details also picks All teams ). The team details email tells each speaker who is on their team, its code name, emoji and break categories. Places allocated goes to an institution representative when their link is sent; Institution registered goes to an institution's contact when it registers (always sent). See registration.md . Delivery status (webhook)  Every message carries an X-CrabbyTab-Ref header. If the server has EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET , point your provider (or a small adapter) at POST /api/email/webhook , signed with an HMAC-SHA256 of the body in X-CrabbyTab-Signature . Campaign history then shows each address's latest status (delivered, bounce, open, and so on). Without the secret the endpoint is off; the settings panel shows whether it is configured. No provider is built in. SMS relay  The server has an SMS hook: with SMS_WEBHOOK_URL (https) and SMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET , an SMS would be posted, signed, to a relay you control (Twilio, Vonage, a gateway). Nothing sends SMS yet ; it is an interface for future work. Phone numbers collected at registration must be in international format. Tips  Use an SMTP provider that authenticates your sending domain (SPF/DKIM) and set SMTP_FROM to an address on that domain. Check your provider's daily limit against teams × speakers × rounds. Emails are plain text only. Differences from Tabbycat  SMTP is the only built-in transport; delivery status needs your own webhook adapter. No browser push notifications. Sends are capped at 100 recipients each. More: email-notifications.md , public-pages-and-notifications.md .

x: Staff and roles  CrabbyTab uses Firebase Authentication (email and password). There is no open sign-up : an account is created either by the site operator in the Firebase console or by accepting a staff invitation (below). Users sign in at /login , reset a forgotten password at /forgot-password and change it at /account/password (account menu). Roles  Role How someone gets it Can do Global administrator UID listed in the server variable FIREBASE_ADMIN_UIDS Everything, on every tournament. The only role that can create tournaments , import a DebateXML archive and open the demo (Tournaments hub). Tournament owner Created the tournament (or first uploaded it) Everything on that tournament, including changing its admins list. Tournament administrator In the tournament's admins list, or given Tournament administrator on Tournament access Everything on that tournament (Tabbycat's tab director): setup, draws, allocation, results, releases, private URLs, email, API tokens, backups, audit log. Cannot change the owner or the admins list. Data-entry staff Given Data-entry staff on Tournament access What their permission groups allow (below), capped by the tournament's staff access level. Participant (no account) Private URL (and passcode) Own draw, ballots, feedback, self check-in. See Private URLs and portals . Public (no account) — Released public pages and enabled public forms only. See Public pages and releases . Signed-out visitors are never administrators, even for a tournament saved on their device. Global administrators  On every sign-in the server compares the account's UID with FIREBASE_ADMIN_UIDS and adds or removes the globalAdmin custom claim; firestore.rules trust that claim. After changing the variable, redeploy and have the person sign in again. Giving people access  Everything is on Admin → Assistants (the page is titled Tournament access , also at /{slug}/staff ), administrators only. Staff roles live in the cloud, so the tournament must have been uploaded. Invite by email (works with or without an account)  Under Invite by email , enter up to 50 addresses (separated by spaces, commas, semicolons or new lines), pick the role and how long the link stays valid (1–30 days, default 7), then Send invitations . Each address receives a single-use link to /invite . The invitee signs in (existing account) or chooses a name and password (at least 8 characters); the server creates the account for exactly the invited address and grants the role in one step. A role is granted only to an account with the invited email; an existing higher role is never lowered. The list shows open invitations (pending or expired) with delivery status. Resend issues a new link (the old one stops working) and restarts the expiry; Revoke stops it at once. If an email cannot be sent (no SMTP, or the provider refused it), the invitation is still created and its link is shown once so you can share it another way. Only a hash of the link is stored; to get a new link, resend. The staff list does not refresh by itself when someone accepts; reload the page. Assign existing accounts  Under Assign existing accounts , enter up to 100 email addresses of existing accounts, choose Data-entry staff (default) or Tournament administrator , and Assign selected access . Unknown addresses are reported as not found; no account directory is exposed. Assigned staff see the tournament on the Tournaments hub. Removing someone (bin icon, then confirm) deletes only their staff assignment; the owner and the tournament's admins list are not changed here. Uploads never change the owner or administrators of a cloud tournament. Permissions  Each data-entry staff member has one or more permission groups (tick them under the person in Assigned to this tournament , then Save groups ). A member with no group ticked gets the Tabulation assistant set. Changes apply to the person's next request. Names must be unique and conflicts.edit needs conflicts.view . Saving recomputes every data-entry member's permissions at once. A member of a deleted group keeps the group id but gets nothing from it. Staff access level  Staff access and private-URL ballots → Data-entry staff access caps every data-entry member. It is a tournament setting, so it reaches the server with the next upload. Level Effect All areas (default) No cap Results entry and draw display Removes Motions before release Results entry only Also removes Draw display before release and Edit adjudicator allocations No access Every data-entry account is refused by every staff route and by the Firestore rules The same card holds the private-URL ballot and feedback switches; see Ballots and results and Private URLs and portals . Public form settings on this page are covered in Public pages and releases . What data-entry staff see and do  Data. Staff receive a filtered copy of the tournament from the server: no owner/admin details, no private URL keys or passcodes, no speaker or adjudicator emails or phone numbers, no audit log. Conflicts, scores and feedback contents only with the matching permission. Unreleased motions only with Motions before release ; draft draws never; confirmed unreleased draws only with Draw display before release (otherwise only released or confirmed rounds for ballot entry); unrevealed panels only with Edit adjudicator allocations . Results. Ballots and debate points reach their device only for rounds they may see: every round with standings.view ; rounds whose results are released; for ballot staff also rounds still being entered and completed rounds that are not silent. Sidebar. Links follow their permissions: Setup (Institutions, Teams, Adjudicators, Diversity, Code names, and Conflicts with conflicts.view ); the round's Availability ( checkins.edit ), Allocation ( allocation.edit ) and Display ( draw.display ); Results; Feedback ( feedback.enter or feedback.view ); Standings, Break and Analytics ( standings.view ). Pages are also checked when opened directly. Administrator-only pages: Draw, Configuration, Assistants, Private URLs, Email, Audit log, Data exports, Rehearsal, API access, Registration, Schedule, and the Venues, Motions, Speaker categories, Adjudicator requirements and Room preferences setup pages. On the Break page, changing categories, generating the break and overrides stay administrator work; preformed panels too. Ballot confirmation. Staff with Confirm others' ballots confirm on the Results page by review or by blind re-entry (confirmed only if it matches). Nobody confirms their own entry. Refused: unpublished draws, cancelled or completed rounds, advanced eliminations and rounds whose results are released, and a version that is no longer the latest. Staff confirmations are recorded on the ballot, not in the audit log. Syncing. Their Upload sends only the records their permissions cover. A record changed by someone else in the meantime, or made from an outdated copy, is refused and kept on their device; allocations are checked per round (no adjudicator twice, no change to closed rounds or confirmed debates) and all-or-nothing per round. Details  Server enforcement: the three staff routes ( assistant-data , data-entry-sync , assistant-ballots ) re-read the staff record inside each write transaction, so narrowing someone's groups applies to their next write. The Firestore rules check the same permissions on the two direct live writes staff make (ballot create, check-in update). Hidden links are never the only barrier. See Security model . Invitation links are {tournament}.{invitation}.{secret} in the URL fragment (never sent to server logs); wrong tokens are throttled (30 failures per hour per address) and account creation is limited to 10 per address per hour. For defence in depth, turn off client sign-up in the Firebase console (Authentication → Settings → User actions). Invitations are only for cloud tournaments. Deleting a tournament does not delete its server-only records (invitations, custom groups). API tokens cannot change staff or group membership. See API and tokens . Differences from Tabbycat  Equity leaves out room-constraint and participant-contact permissions (room preferences, emails and phone numbers stay administrator-only).
