Testing  CrabbyTab's tests are Vitest unit tests. They run in Node, need no browser, no Firebase project and no credentials, and are deterministic. This page covers how to run them, where they live, the differential harness against Tabbycat, the translation checks, and what is not covered. Running the checks  The scripts in package.json : Command What it runs npm run test (or npm test ) vitest run : every *.test.ts file once npm run lint next lint with .eslintrc.json ( next/core-web-vitals ) npm run build next build , the production build npm run i18n:check the translation catalogue tests (see below ) npm run i18n:new -- <code> creates a new language catalogue from English Other useful commands (not scripts, run through npx ): npx vitest  watch mode npx vitest run src/lib/draw  one folder npx vitest run src/lib/ballots/result.test.ts  one file npx vitest run -t "low-point"  tests whose name matches npx tsc --noEmit  full type check, tests included tsconfig.json includes every .ts and .tsx file, so tsc --noEmit type-checks the tests and the tools/ folder too. Continuous integration  .github/workflows/ci.yml runs on every push and pull request, on Node 22: npm ci → npm run lint → npx tsc --noEmit → npm run test → npm run build All five must pass. CI needs no Firebase project, Docker or Python. Setup  vitest.config.ts : environment: "node" (there is no DOM; nothing renders React), globals: true ( describe , it , expect without imports, though most files import them from vitest ), the @ alias points to src/ , as in the app. There is no include pattern, so Vitest's default applies: every *.test.ts file in the repository outside node_modules , including tools/ . There are about 250 test files. Where tests live  Tests sit next to the code they test, named <module>.test.ts . The main groups: Folder Covers src/lib/draw/ draw generation: two-team and BP power pairing, brackets and pull-ups, conflict avoidance, minimum-cost and blossom matching, side allocation, round robin, eliminations, N teams per room, venue and adjudicator allocation, seeded reproducibility src/lib/standings/ , src/lib/breakqual/ standings, precedence and tie handling, break qualification rules src/lib/ballots/ , src/lib/scoring/ ballot validation and aggregation, winner rules, voting and individual ballots src/lib/csv/ , src/lib/participants/ , src/lib/registration/ CSV import and export, participant validation, registration src/lib/publicView/ , src/lib/seo/ the public projection, release rules, caching, sitemap and robots rules src/lib/email/ , src/lib/api/v1/ email recipients and templates, the REST API src/lib/*.test.ts private URLs and passcodes, rate limits, staff permissions, tournament access, audit chain, security headers, Firestore rule text (below) src/features/tournament/application/ the application commands: draws and regeneration, ballots and confirmation, breaks, round completion, live sync, cloud sync and conflicts, backups, DebateXML import and export, whole-tournament lifecycles ( lifecycle.bp.test.ts , lifecycle.wsdc.test.ts ) src/features/tournament/infrastructure/ Firestore repositories against an in-memory fake, including uploadScale.test.ts (a synthetic 1000-team upload) src/app/api/**/ a few route handlers, with Firebase Admin mocked src/lib/i18n/ , tools/i18n/ translations tools/tabbycat-diff/ the differential test against Tabbycat Sample CSV files for manual testing of the import pages are in testdata/ (institutions, teams, adjudicators, venues, motions). No automated test uses them. Writing tests  AGENTS.md section 11 sets the expectations. In practice: Test pure functions and application commands with explicit inputs. Keep tournament logic out of React components so it can be tested here. Mock external services. Commands take a repository or dependencies object; tests pass in-memory fakes or vi.mock the Firebase modules. Never require a live Firebase project. For anything random, pass a fixed seed and assert that the same inputs and seed give the same output. Test invalid and infeasible cases, not only the happy path: no feasible draw, side limits, duplicate records, missing results (not zero), malformed CSV, quoted fields and embedded newlines. Keep tests independent of execution order and of the clock; inject timestamps. When a test pins a Tabbycat behaviour, say so in the test name or a comment and point at the Tabbycat source. Differential testing against Tabbycat  tools/tabbycat-diff/ runs the same tournaments through the official Tabbycat (v2.12.1) and through CrabbyTab's own libraries, and compares the results rule by rule. Full documentation: tools/tabbycat-diff/README.md ; latest findings: report/REPORT.md . What it compares  For each fixture, tabbycatDiff.test.ts imports the fixture's DebateXML with CrabbyTab's importer, applies Tabbycat's effective preferences (from the golden file), and computes through the real libraries: Area Compared Standings every team and speaker metric both engines compute, ranks and the reply tab, after every round. Tabbycat's null (no results) never equals a CrabbyTab 0 . Draws a draw for every round from the rounds before it, over eight seeds: room count, coverage, bracket composition, pull-ups, side imbalance, institution clashes, repeat pairings, side-cap violations, BP position cost and byes. Draws often have several valid answers, so they are compared by these properties, not room by room. Breaks breaking and reserve teams per category, in priority order, and break ranks Adjudicator allocation hard conflicts, chairs, panel sizes, history repeats and the sum of chair scores, using CrabbyTab's ports of Tabbycat's Voting and Consensus Hungarian allocators Every discrepancy must have a human verdict in known-differences.json : rule difference , CrabbyTab defect , configuration difference or valid alternative . The test fails when a discrepancy has no verdict, or when the set of discrepancies or verdicts differs from the committed report/report.json (something was fixed or something regressed). It also fails if a fixture has no golden file. Two smaller tests sit beside it: compare.test.ts (the comparison rules themselves) and tieOrder.test.ts (given Tabbycat's fixed tie order, CrabbyTab pairs exactly Tabbycat's rooms and byes in the twoteam-odd-ties fixture). Not compared: elimination rounds, feedback, motions and venues. Debate importance is 0 on both sides. Fixtures and golden files  Path What it is fixtures/<name>/tournament.xml , config.json the tournament (DebateXML) plus what DebateXML cannot carry fixtures/generate.ts the seeded generator that writes the fixtures golden/<name>.tabbycat.json Tabbycat's output, committed so CI needs no Docker or Python tabbycat/ the Tabbycat runner ( run_tabbycat.py ), Dockerfile , docker-compose.yml , run-native.sh The three fixtures are bp-uneven (BP, 26 teams with byes, three break categories, iron-person speeches), australs-voting (Australs two-team rules, voting panels with splits, replies) and twoteam-odd-ties (19 teams, wins only, many ties). Regenerating  All commands run from the repository root. In order: Fixtures (only after editing FIXTURES in fixtures/generate.ts ): node tools/tabbycat-diff/fixtures/generate.ts This runs a TypeScript file directly, so it needs a Node version with type stripping on by default (22.18 or later). The output is byte-identical for the same seed. Node prints a harmless MODULE_TYPELESS_PACKAGE_JSON warning. Golden files (Tabbycat's side; after changing fixtures or the Tabbycat version). With Docker: docker compose -f tools/tabbycat-diff/tabbycat/docker-compose.yml run --rm --build tabbycat docker compose -f tools/tabbycat-diff/tabbycat/docker-compose.yml down -v Without Docker you need Python 3.11, git and the PostgreSQL binaries: PG_BIN="/c/Program Files/PostgreSQL/18/bin" tools/tabbycat-diff/tabbycat/run-native.sh The native script clones Tabbycat into ~/.cache/crabbytab-tabbycat-diff (override with TABBYCAT_DIFF_WORK ) and runs a throwaway local PostgreSQL cluster on port 54329, deleted afterwards. The first run takes about seven minutes. The committed golden files came from the native route; the Docker route has not been run yet. Report (after reviewing a change in the discrepancies, and adding verdicts for new ones to known-differences.json ): TABBYCAT_DIFF_WRITE=1 npx vitest run tools/tabbycat-diff This rewrites report/REPORT.md and report/report.json . Do not edit them by hand. On PowerShell, set the variable first: $env:TABBYCAT_DIFF_WRITE = "1"; npx vitest run tools/tabbycat-diff . None of these is an npm script. Translation checks  npm run i18n:check runs vitest run src/lib/i18n : catalogues.test.ts : every catalogue has every English key and no unknown keys, every plural category the language needs, and the same {placeholders} and <tags> as English; config.test.ts : locale matching, selection order, text direction and the pre-paint script; translate.test.ts : loading, fallback, interpolation, plurals, rich text and formatting. The same tests run in npm test , so adding an English string without adding the key to every other catalogue fails CI. npm run i18n:new -- <code> writes src/lib/i18n/messages/locales/<code>.json through tools/i18n/newLanguage.test.ts ; in a normal test run that file only checks the template builder. See Languages and translations . Firestore rules  There is no Firestore emulator setup and the rules are not executed in CI (the emulator needs Java and firebase-tools ). Two tests read firestore.rules as text instead: src/lib/liveRules.test.ts keeps the field lists data-entry staff may write directly (live ballots, check-ins) equal to ASSISTANT_LIVE_BALLOT_FIELDS / ASSISTANT_LIVE_CHECK_IN_FIELDS in src/lib/dataEntrySync.ts ; src/lib/serverOnlyRules.test.ts checks that the serverOnly namespace (invitations, registration, custom permission groups) is excluded from the administrator rule and denied to every client. Before deploying rule changes, check them by hand in the Firebase console's Rules Playground with the cases listed in live-collaboration.md . Not covered  No React component tests (the environment is Node, and no DOM testing library is installed). No end-to-end browser tests. Check UI changes by hand with npm run dev . No executed Firestore rules tests (see above). Tabbycat differential coverage is limited to the three fixtures and the areas listed above. A passing build and test run do not prove tournament logic is correct or fair; add a test for the rule you changed.

Contributing  Contributions are welcome: bug fixes, tournament-workflow improvements, accessibility, translations, documentation, tests and ideas. This page summarises how work flows into CrabbyTab. The source documents are: CONTRIBUTING.md : setting up, making a change, opening a pull request. AGENTS.md : the engineering rules, for people and AI coding agents alike. CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md . SECURITY.md : report vulnerabilities privately with GitHub's Report a vulnerability , never in a public issue. Contributions are distributed under AGPL-3.0-or-later . Branches and pull requests  Branch Role beta Where development is integrated. Feature branches start here and pull requests target it. main The default branch on GitHub. It receives beta when a release is cut; it is currently behind beta . feature branches One per change, named after it (for example claude/p2-results-pages ). Merged into beta by pull request. The workflow: For a substantial change, open an issue first so the scope can be agreed. Branch from beta . Keep the branch to one fix or feature. If beta moves on, merge it into your branch. Make the change, with tests and documentation (below). Run the checks locally (below). Open a pull request into beta using the template: summary, related issue, changes, verification, screenshots for UI changes, and any configuration, data or migration implications. CI runs lint, the type check, the tests and the build on every push and pull request; all must pass. Local setup  Node.js 22 ( package.json sets engines.node to 22.x ) and npm. See Installation and local development . npm ci  install exactly what package-lock.json records npm run dev  http://localhost:3000 Copy .env.example to .env.local only if your change needs Firebase or email. Ordinary tests need no credentials. Engineering rules in short  From AGENTS.md : Read first. Inspect the existing code before changing it; the code is the source of truth. Reuse existing helpers rather than duplicating them. Keep changes focused; do not redesign unrelated pages. Local-first. Draws, allocation, standings and validation run in the browser as deterministic functions, separate from React components. Do not add paid services or remote computation. Tournament integrity. Never silently relax a hard draw constraint, discard a team, or treat a missing result as zero. Report constraints that cannot be met. Randomness takes an explicit seed, so the same inputs and seed give the same draw. Do not claim a draw is optimal unless the algorithm proves it. Document trade-offs. Heuristics, tie-breaking rules and known differences from Tabbycat are written down in the code and in docs/ (see tabbycat-parity-plan.md , "Still different from Tabbycat"). Security. Enforce access in firestore.rules or server routes, never only in the UI. Keep secrets out of the client bundle. Do not weaken the rules to work around a bug. Never log tokens or participant data. Data. Validate before saving; use transactions or batches for multi-step writes; never silently overwrite newer changes; keep stored data backward compatible. UI. Accessible labels, keyboard use, visible focus, status not by colour alone, loading/empty/error states, and protection against double submission. New user-facing text must be translatable (below). Dependencies. Use the existing stack (Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind 3, Firebase, lucide-react, PapaParse, Vitest). Do not add a dependency for something small, and never upgrade a major version as part of an unrelated change. Git. Do not rewrite history on shared branches or commit secrets, .env.local , build output or node_modules . Code style  TypeScript throughout. Avoid any ; prefer explicit types or unknown with narrowing. Do not loosen tsconfig.json or disable lint rules to make a change pass. Small functions with clear names. Comments explain why (a domain rule, a Tabbycat reference, a trade-off), not what the code does. Business logic lives in src/lib/** and src/features/tournament/application/ ; Firestore access in src/features/tournament/infrastructure/ and server routes under src/app/api/ . See Architecture . Components are server components unless they need interactivity or browser APIs ( "use client" ). Styling with Tailwind and the shared components in src/components/ui/ ; see design-system.md . For right-to-left languages use logical utilities ( ms-* , pe-* , text-start ). npm run lint must be clean. Tests  Every change to business logic needs a test: draws and constraints, byes and side balance, standings and tie-breaks, ballots and scoring, breaks, CSV import, permissions and error cases. Include the infeasible case, not just the happy path, and a fixed-seed reproducibility check for anything random. Before opening a pull request, run what CI runs: npm run lint npx tsc --noEmit npm run test npm run build If your change alters draws, standings, breaks or allocation, the Tabbycat differential test may report a changed discrepancy. Review it, record a verdict in tools/tabbycat-diff/known-differences.json , and regenerate the report. Details, and how to run single files: Testing . If you cannot run a check, say so in the pull request and list what you did run. Security model  Who can read and write what, and where that is enforced. This page is for contributors and people deploying CrabbyTab. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md . There are two enforcement points: firestore.rules for everything the browser reads or writes directly with the Firebase client SDK. Server routes ( src/app/api/** ) for everything else. They use the Firebase Admin SDK, which ignores the rules, so each route checks the caller itself. Hiding a link in the UI is never the barrier. Identities  Identity How it is recognised Notes Global administrator globalAdmin custom claim on the Firebase account The claim is set from the FIREBASE_ADMIN_UIDS environment variable by GET /api/auth/access ( src/lib/globalAdmin.ts ). Server routes check the environment variable directly; Firestore rules trust the claim. Tournament administrator Tournament ownerId , an admins map entry set to true , or staff/{uid}.role == "admin" Global administrators count as administrators of every tournament. Data-entry staff staff/{uid}.role == "dataEntry" Limited by permission groups and the tournament's access level. See Staff and roles . Participant Private URL key + passcode No account. Public visitor None Sees only the published snapshot. Integration Bearer API token Hashed, scoped, revocable. See API and tokens . Accounts are Firebase email/password accounts. The app has no self-sign-up page; staff accounts can be created by accepting a staff invitation ( /api/invitations ). Firestore rules  Read firestore.rules itself before changing any client read or write. Path Read Write tournaments/{id} Administrators and data-entry staff Create: global admins only. Update: administrators, who cannot change ownerId ; only the owner (or a global admin) may change admins . Delete: administrators. tournaments/{id}/{collection}/{doc} (any collection not listed below: rounds, teams, adjudicators, debates, ballots, feedback, motions, venues, ... ) Administrators Administrators .../ballots/{id} — Also: data-entry staff may create their own unconfirmed, undiscarded ballot ( submitterType "tabroom" , own uid, whitelisted fields, syncVersion 1, existing non-deleted debate of the same round), with results.enter .../teams/{id} , .../adjudicators/{id} — Also: data-entry staff may update only check-in fields ( checkedIn , checkedInAt , roundAvailability , roundAvailabilityAt , checkInHistory ≤ 50, syncVersion +1) on non-deleted records, with checkins.edit .../staff/{uid} Administrators Administrators .../syncConflicts/{id} Administrators Create only; never update or delete .../auditEvents/{id} Administrators Create only, attributed to the writer or to system ; never update or delete .../auditReleases/** Nobody Nobody (server only) .../serverOnly/** Nobody Nobody (server only) .../data/{doc} Administrators Administrators tournamentSlugs/{slug} Any signed-in user Global admins, or the owner / admins -map administrator of the tournament the slug points to (checked against the post-write tournament) users/{uid} That user That user publicViews/** Nobody Nobody (server only) Anything else (including top-level apiRateLimits ) Global admins Global admins Notes: Data-entry staff never read tournament subcollections directly. Their copy comes redacted from /api/tournaments/{id}/assistant-data (no private URL keys, passcodes, emails, phone numbers; conflicts and scores only with the right permission). Their direct writes also require assistantMay(...) : the permission is in their staff document's permissions list (missing list = the default set) and the tournament's assistantAccess is not "none" . Firestore combines rules with OR. Global admins match the final catch-all, so append-only rules do not bind them. The tournament catch-all matches one level only. Deeper paths (for example auditReleases/{id}/events ) fall through to the global-admin rule. staff documents with role: "admin" make someone an administrator, and any administrator may write staff . So "only the owner may change admins " protects the admins map, not the set of administrators as a whole. The staff route also lets any administrator assign the admin role. Server-written collections under the admin catch-all. apiTokens , emailCampaigns and notificationLog are written by server routes, but they are not excluded from the catch-all, so tournament administrators can also read and write them directly from the browser. In practice: administrators can read API token records (name, scopes, creator, timestamps and the SHA-256 tokenHash ; the secret is never stored), create or edit token records directly, edit or delete email history, and edit or delete notification log entries (which could make an automatic notification send again or not at all). Administrators already have full control of the tournament, so this grants no new access, but these records are not tamper-proof against administrators. There is no rules emulator in CI. src/lib/serverOnlyRules.test.ts and src/lib/liveRules.test.ts check the rules text (the serverOnly exclusion and deny rule; the staff field lists match src/lib/dataEntrySync.ts ). Test rule changes in the Firebase console Rules Playground before deploying. See docs/live-collaboration.md for the checklist. Never loosen the rules to work around a bug. Server-only documents  tournaments/{id}/serverOnly/** is denied to every client and only touched by server routes: Document Contents staffInvitations/items/* Staff invitations (token stored as a hash; administrators never see it) staffPermissionGroups Custom permission groups emailSettings Reply-To and saved email templates publicForms Public-form password as a salted scrypt hash ( src/lib/publicFormsPassword.ts ) Registration settings, submissions, representatives, team invitations, transfers Registration ( src/lib/registration/ ); link tokens stored as hashes Also server-only: auditReleases (released audit snapshots), publicViews (public snapshots) and the top-level apiRateLimits . Server routes  Administrator routes verify the Firebase ID token and resolve the role with authorizeTournamentAdministrator ( src/lib/tournamentAdminAuth.ts ); some re-check inside the write ( assertStillAdministrator ). Staff routes ( assistant-data , data-entry-sync , assistant-ballots ) use authorizeDataEntryStaff and re-read the staff document inside each write transaction ( currentDataEntryPermissions in src/lib/staffAccessServer.ts ), so revoking a group applies to the next record. Synced records are whitelisted per field ( DATA_ENTRY_FIELDS in src/lib/dataEntrySync.ts ); staff ballots are always unconfirmed; guarded fields (conflicts, scores, panels) are accepted only with the matching permission and from a copy based on the current syncVersion . Nobody confirms their own ballot. Private portals ( /api/private/team , /api/private/sync ) find the participant by private URL key and compare the passcode in constant time. Teams cannot submit ballots; adjudicators only for their own debates; feedback only between people who sat in that debate. Email delivery webhook ( /api/email/webhook ) requires an HMAC signature with EMAIL_WEBHOOK_SECRET and is disabled without it. Payload caps , for example: data-entry sync 4 MB and 5,000 records per collection; private sync 100 queued items; public forms 64 KB. Staff permissions  Permissions ( src/lib/staffPermissions.ts ): results.enter , results.confirm_others , ballots.intake , feedback.enter , checkins.edit , participants.edit , draw.display , motions.display , conflicts.view , conflicts.edit , feedback.view , adjudicators.scores_edit , allocation.edit , standings.view . Built-in groups: Tabulation assistant (default), Ballot desk, Check-in desk, Feedback desk, Equity, Adjudication core. Administrators can add up to 30 custom groups (stored server-only; PUT /api/tournaments/{id}/staff/groups validates them and recomputes every staff member's stored permissions in one transaction). The tournament's access level ( assistantAccess : all areas, results and draw display, results only, none) caps every group. none refuses every staff route and the two direct rule-based writes. Staff documents created before groups existed have no permissions field and keep the default set. Details: docs/staff-access.md . Passcodes and secrets  Secret Stored as Compared by Participant private URL key and passcode ( privateUrlKey , privatePasscode ) Plain text on team / adjudicator records (administrators can read them; printed on slips) passcodesMatch ( src/lib/passcode.ts ): both values SHA-256 hashed, then timingSafeEqual , so timing reveals neither length nor prefix API token ( ct_live_ + 64 hex) SHA-256 hash ( tokenHash ), shown once at creation Hash lookup ( src/lib/apiTokens.ts ) Staff invitation, registration links Hashes in serverOnly Server-side Public-form password Salted scrypt hash in serverOnly/publicForms timingSafeEqual Service account, SMTP password, webhook secret Server environment variables only — Participant devices remember portal passcodes in localStorage. Rate limits  Durable limits are sliding one-hour windows stored in the top-level apiRateLimits collection, keyed by a SHA-256 hash of the identity ( src/lib/privateTeamRateLimit.ts ). Client addresses come from x-real-ip / x-forwarded-for , which Vercel sets. Where Limit Private portals, per private link ( team , sync ) 300 requests / hour Private portals, failed attempts (unknown key or wrong passcode) per address 100 / hour; checked before the key lookup Staff invitations 30 failed tokens and 10 new accounts per address per hour Public forms 30 failed passwords per address per hour; 240 submissions per address and 6,000 per tournament per hour Public registration 30 failed links per address; 40 per address per tournament, 60 per address, 600 per tournament per hour v1 API ( src/lib/api/v1/rateLimit.ts ) 600 requests/min per address, 60 anonymous/min per address, 300/min per token (in memory, per server instance); 1,000 writes/hour per token and 120 /me lookups/hour per address (durable) The in-memory API limits are a burst guard per serverless instance, not a global quota. API tokens  Created and revoked only through /api/tournaments/{id}/api-tokens (administrators). Scopes ( src/lib/apiScopes.ts ): read:public — only what the public site shows. Cannot be combined with other scopes. read:{resource} and write:{resource} for tournament , rounds , participants , venues , breaks , draws , results , feedback , checkins ; read:standings and read:staff only. write implies read . No token can grant staff access. Tokens stay valid until revoked, including after the administrator who created them loses access. See the note above on direct browser access to apiTokens . What is public  Only the public projection ( src/lib/publicView/projection.ts ), built on the server at publish time. It copies an allowlist of fields per collection and applies the release settings: Published (when released / switched on) Never published Tournament name, slug, format, preferences (minus private speaker categories; schedule only when released; room category descriptions only when marked public) Owner, admin list, owner email Rounds that are visible (draw released, results released, or in a released tab), with their status flags Unreleased or locked draws, cancelled rounds Debates of visible rounds: teams, sides, room, bracket; panels only once revealed; points and speaker totals only with released results Unrevealed panels, results of silent or unreleased rounds Confirmed ballots of rounds with public results; speaker scores only when team speaks are released; per-adjudicator sheets and split adjudicators only when switched on and the panel is revealed Unconfirmed or discarded ballots Teams that appear publicly (in a public debate, a released break, released participants list or side allocations): name or code name, speakers, institution and emoji if switched on, public speaker categories Private URL keys, passcodes, emails, phone numbers, private speaker categories, conflicts Adjudicators on revealed panels or released lists: name, institution if switched on, trainee / core / breaking flags only when that list is released Base and test scores, feedback, score history, conflicts Released motions; info slides of rounds with released info slides Unreleased motions Break categories; the generated break only when released Break overrides, unreleased breaks Institutions only when their list is released; rooms (name, category, capacity, accessibility, http(s) links) — Aggregates computed on the server: tabs with top-N limits, adjudicator tab, diversity, feedback progress (feedback is read only when one of these is on) Raw feedback (the feedback collection is always empty) See Public pages and releases . Browser and headers  securityHeaders.mjs (applied to every path by next.config.mjs ) sets a Content-Security-Policy ( default-src 'self' ; connections only to self and Firebase endpoints; frame-ancestors 'self' , object-src 'none' , base-uri 'self' , form-action 'self' ; script-src allows 'unsafe-inline' for Next.js bootstrap scripts, plus 'unsafe-eval' in development), X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN , X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff , Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin and a Permissions-Policy that disables camera, microphone and geolocation. src/lib/securityHeaders.test.ts covers it. The organiser's working copy in IndexedDB holds everything an administrator can see, including passcodes and feedback. Use trusted devices and clear site data on shared computers. Signed-out viewers are never treated as administrators. Untrusted input  CSV and DebateXML files are parsed as data only. DebateXML with DOCTYPE or entity declarations is refused and record counts are capped. CSV exports escape formula-like cells. Room links are published only if they are http(s). Known gaps  Participant passcodes and private URL keys are stored in plain text (administrators can read them). apiTokens , emailCampaigns and notificationLog are writable by administrators from the browser (see above). Firestore rules are not executed in CI (text checks only). State rules (locked ballots, completed rounds) are checked on the device for administrators' live writes, not by the rules. script-src allows inline scripts. FAQ and troubleshooting  Common questions from organisers, and what to do when something looks wrong. Each answer links to the page with the full explanation. Accounts and access  I signed in but cannot create a tournament. Only global administrators can create, import or load a demo tournament. Your account's UID must be in FIREBASE_ADMIN_UIDS on the server, the server needs Firebase Admin credentials, and the current firestore.rules must be deployed. After the variable changes, redeploy and sign out and in again. See Staff and roles . How do people get an account? There is no open sign-up. Either create the account in the Firebase console, or invite people from the tournament's Staff page: they get an email link, choose a name and password, and receive the role in one step. If email is not set up, the invitation link is shown once on the Staff page so you can send it yourself. See Staff and roles . Adding a staff member says the account was not found. Assigning directly only works for an existing account. Send an invitation instead. A staff member cannot see the tournament. The tournament must have been uploaded at least once, and the person must have a role on it. Ask them to reload /tournaments . The Staff page does not refresh by itself when someone accepts an invitation; reload it. A data-entry staff member cannot see the draw, motions or standings. Their permission groups and the tournament's staff access level decide what they see. Check them on Tournament access , then upload (the access level is a tournament setting). See Staff and roles . Working offline, uploading and syncing  Does CrabbyTab work without internet? Yes, for the tab room. Each device keeps a full working copy in the browser and computes draws, allocations and standings itself. Offline changes stay on the device (live changes are queued and sent on reconnect). What needs the internet: uploading, releases (they are refused while offline), public pages, private URLs and email. See Backups, restore and cloud sync . My changes are not on the public page. Public pages show the last published cloud copy, not your device. Check, in order: The cloud status pill in the top bar. N changes not uploaded means they are only on this device: use Upload now . N upload conflicts or Upload incomplete means nothing was published; resolve or upload again. That the thing is released. Draws, results, motions, tabs and breaks each need their own release, and the matching switch under Configuration → Public visibility must be on. See Public pages and releases . Open public pages check for updates every 45 seconds. Reload to see a change at once. Account menu → Republish public pages rebuilds the public pages from the cloud copy. If this device has changes that are not uploaded, it asks whether to upload them first. Changes from another device are missing. Ballots, draws, allocations and check-ins sync live between administrator devices for the active round , within seconds. Everything else (settings, rounds and their releases, motions, rooms, breaks, feedback) needs an Upload now on the other device, then Download and compare or a reload here. Corrections to earlier rounds also arrive only after a reload or download. Check the pill says Live and that live updates are not paused on either device. The pill shows sync conflicts. A record changed both here and in the cloud. Open Resolve sync conflicts (cloud status menu or account menu), compare the two versions, and pick Keep mine or Use cloud for each. Then upload. Nothing is lost: every replaced cloud version is archived, and account menu → Export sync recovery downloads them all. The pill shows double confirmations. Two devices confirmed different ballots for the same debate before seeing each other's. Open that debate's ballots and discard the version that should not count. CrabbyTab never picks one for you. "The new draw is saved on this device, but updating the cloud copy did not finish." Press Upload now . The upload completes the change. "Could not save … locally". The browser's storage is full or blocked (some private-browsing modes do this). Export a backup (account menu), upload if you can, then free disk space or use a normal window. CrabbyTab retries with the next change. I cleared my browser data or changed computers. If the tournament was uploaded, sign in and open it again: the cloud copy loads. Otherwise restore your last JSON backup (account menu → Restore tournament backup ). Export backups regularly during the event. Public pages and private URLs  The public link shows nothing or "not found". A tournament that has never been uploaded exists only on your device. Upload it once; then the public URL works for everyone. Participants' private links do not work. Private URLs read the cloud copy, so new or regenerated links work only after you upload. Regenerate all private keys stops every link already handed out. See Private URLs and portals . A private link says too many requests. Links are rate-limited (per link, and failed passcodes per network). Wait for the retry time shown. A whole venue on one network typing wrong passcodes can trigger the network limit. Teams cannot see the motion on their portal. Release the motions for the round on the Motions page and make sure the release has been uploaded (releases upload and publish in one step when you are online). Emailing private URLs is refused. Either a participant has no private URL or passcode yet (generate them on the Private URLs page), or one email address belongs to two different participants. Fix the duplicate address and try again. Will search engines index our tournament or participants' links? Private URLs, the projector and every tab-room page are excluded from crawling and marked noindex . For public pages, choose Search engines under Configuration → Public visibility: every page, only the public homepage, or none. Search engines may ignore noindex , so it is not a privacy control, and the sitemap is refreshed at most every six hours. See Caching, indexing and performance . Draws  "Number of teams (…) must be divisible by …". Mark the right teams available for the round, add a swing team (Draw page, Swing teams ), or set Bye team selection method to Lowest ranked or Random . See Rounds and draws . The draw failed because of a side limit. Maximum allowed side imbalance is a hard limit. Raise it (0 turns it off) or adjust the draw by hand. Maximum times per side does not block a draw. "Every team needs a seed for a seeded draw." Seeded and round-robin draws need a seed for every team. Set them in the draw setup panel on the Draw page, or import them with the team seed column. Can I regenerate a draw? Yes. If ballots exist you are warned that they will be discarded (kept in history, no longer counting). A confirmed or released draw needs a reason. Only regenerate if the round was not debated as drawn. Can I run a format with three, five or six teams per room? Yes: the N teams per room format. As in Tabbycat, it supports random and manual draws only; power-paired, seeded and round-robin draws, side rules and generated elimination draws are refused. A random draw puts any remainder in a short last room, or gives byes if a bye method is set. See Tournament setup and formats . Results  I can't confirm a ballot I entered. With double entry on, a different person must check it. "… is declared the winner with a lower total. Low-point wins are not allowed." Fix the scores, or set Deciding the winner (tournament settings, results rules) to allow low-point wins if your rules permit them. See Ballots and results . "… speaks more than once". Mark the extra speech as an iron-person (ghost) speech. Published results disappeared from the public page. Confirming a changed ballot, or discarding the confirmed one, withdraws the round's results and team speaks release. Check the result and release it again. An adjudicator's private-URL ballot does not show up. Private-URL ballots go to the cloud. For the active round they reach administrator devices live; for other rounds use Download and compare or reload. Depending on Ballots submitted through private URLs , a chair's ballot either counts at once or waits unconfirmed for the tab room. It never replaces a ballot the tab room already confirmed. Language  How do I change the interface language? For yourself: account menu → language (or the language menu on public pages). For participants: Configuration → Public visibility → Public pages and portals language ; a viewer's own choice still wins. All languages other than English are machine-drafted and need review. Emails and some server messages are still in English. See Languages and translations . Hosting and quota  Are we within the free Firestore quota? Public audience size barely matters: public pages are served from cached snapshots. Reads come mainly from opening the tournament on admin devices, uploads, downloads and private-URL use. A 100-team event with a few admin devices stays well inside Spark's 50,000 reads a day. A 1000-team event's first upload is about 10,000 writes, so plan on the Blaze plan for events that size. Upload when you need to, not constantly. See Deploying to Vercel and Firebase and Caching, indexing and performance . Can I run it without Firebase? Without Firebase configured nobody can sign in, so no tournament can be created, and there are no public pages, private URLs, staff accounts or email. In practice a Firebase project is required. Still stuck? Open an issue on GitHub . Never include participant data or credentials.
